With orthonormalization enabled, the propagated Gram matrix must differ from the identity by at most `1e-6` (single precision) or `1e-12` (double precision) per element; unsuccessful corrections stop the calculation. Wavefunctions within this tolerance are left unchanged. Nonfinite or nonpositive orbital norms are rejected even with `none`.

td_out_stat.description:
Write wavefunction and density electron counts, their changes from the initial state, and orthogonality errors to the running log after each electronic evolution step. Electron counts describe the end-of-step state; orthogonality errors before and after correction are separate maxima over all SCF iterations and k points within that step. When half-step retries are enabled, only accepted substeps contribute to these maxima. Orthogonality errors are omitted when `td_orthonormal=none`.

[NOTE] Enabling this output adds density integration and diagnostic communication.

td_max_halvings.description: Maximum number of recursive halvings of an electronic propagation interval when self-consistency fails. Zero disables retries. Each full-step or subdivided trial uses at most `td_scf_nmax` iterations. The smallest internal time step is `td_dt / 2^td_max_halvings`; output times and the physical field profile retain the original `td_dt` grid. A value of 3 allows internal steps down to `td_dt / 8`.

td_scf_nmax.description: Maximum number of self-consistency iterations for each real-time propagation step in PW and LCAO calculations. Must be an integer of at least 2. Convergence can end the iterations early. In PW calculations, when `td_max_halvings` is positive, the limit applies independently to each full-step or subdivided trial. This parameter is independent of `scf_nmax`.

td_out_mag.description:
Write total and atomic magnetic moments to `mag_tot.txt` and `mag_atom.txt` at every step.
* `voronoi`: Integrate magnetization over periodic nearest-atom regions, including vacuum.
* `onsite`: Project onto the smoothed single-zeta numerical atomic orbitals. `onsite_radius` controls their cutoff.
* `none`: Disable these two files.

Total moments always come from the magnetization density. Atomic onsite moments need not sum to the total. Moments follow the ABACUS Pauli convention in Bohr magnetons.

td_out_torque.description:
Write total exchange-correlation and SOC torques to `torque_tot.txt` and the atomic SOC contributions to `torque_atom.txt` at every step. In Hartree atomic units,

$$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{xc}}=\mathrm{i}\sum_{n\boldsymbol{k}}f_{n\boldsymbol{k}}\Braket{\psi_{n\boldsymbol{k}}|\left[\hat{V}_{\mathrm{xc}},\hat{\boldsymbol{S}}\right]|\psi_{n\boldsymbol{k}}},$$

$$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{SOC}}=\mathrm{i}\sum_{n\boldsymbol{k}}f_{n\boldsymbol{k}}\Braket{\psi_{n\boldsymbol{k}}|\left[\hat{V}_{\mathrm{SOC}},\hat{\boldsymbol{S}}\right]|\psi_{n\boldsymbol{k}}}.$$

Here $\hat{\boldsymbol{S}}=\boldsymbol{\sigma}/2$, with $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ the Pauli matrices, and $f_{n\boldsymbol{k}}$ includes occupations and k-point weights. $\hat{V}_{\mathrm{xc}}$ is the spin-dependent exchange-correlation potential, and $\hat{V}_{\mathrm{SOC}}$ is the SOC part of the nonlocal pseudopotential.

The torques describe changes in spin angular momentum $\boldsymbol{S}=\boldsymbol{M}/2$, where $\boldsymbol{M}$ follows the ABACUS Pauli convention. Atomic SOC contributions use the corresponding atomic pseudopotential terms.

td_out_spincur.description:
Write the nine macroscopic spin angular momentum current components to `spincur_tot.txt` at every step. In Hartree atomic units,

$$J_i^a=\frac{1}{2\Omega}\sum_{n\boldsymbol{k}}f_{n\boldsymbol{k}}\Braket{\psi_{n\boldsymbol{k}}|\left\{\hat{v}_i,\hat{S}_a\right\}|\psi_{n\boldsymbol{k}}},\qquad \hat{S}_a=\frac{\sigma_a}{2}.$$

Here $\Omega$ is the cell volume, $f_{n\boldsymbol{k}}$ includes occupations and k-point weights, $\sigma_a$ is a Pauli matrix, and $\hat{v}_i$ is the velocity operator including the nonlocal pseudopotential contribution.

Components are ordered $xx,xy,xz,yx,yy,yz,zx,zy,zz$, with flow direction first and spin polarization second.

lin_solver.description:
Iterative linear solver used for PW real-time propagation.
* `bicgstab`: Biconjugate gradient stabilized (BiCGSTAB) method.
* `cgs`: Conjugate gradient squared (CGS) method.
* `gmres`: Restarted generalized minimal residual (GMRES) method, controlled by `lin_gmres_restart`.

The initial ground-state diagonalization is controlled by `ks_solver`.

lin_precond.description:
Right preconditioner used by PW real-time linear solvers. The Crank-Nicolson operator is $\boldsymbol{L}=\boldsymbol{I}+\mathrm{i}\Delta t\,\boldsymbol{H}/2$, with the propagation Hamiltonian $\boldsymbol{H}$ in Hartree and time step $\Delta t$ in atomic units. Below, $\boldsymbol{M}^{-1}$ denotes the inverse preconditioner and $\boldsymbol{D}$ the kinetic diagonal inverse.
* `kinetic`: Apply $\boldsymbol{M}^{-1}=\boldsymbol{D}$, with diagonal entries $D_{\boldsymbol{G}\boldsymbol{G}}=(1+\mathrm{i}\Delta t\,T_{\boldsymbol{G}}/2)^{-1}$, where $T_{\boldsymbol{G}}=\lVert\boldsymbol{k}+\boldsymbol{G}+\boldsymbol{A}_{\mathrm{mid}}\rVert^2/2$ is the kinetic energy in Hartree. In the velocity gauge, $\boldsymbol{A}_{\mathrm{mid}}=(\boldsymbol{A}_n+\boldsymbol{A}_{n+1})/2$ is the propagation vector potential in Hartree atomic units; in the length gauge, set $\boldsymbol{A}_{\mathrm{mid}}=\boldsymbol{0}$.
* `kinetic_recycle`: Apply $\boldsymbol{M}^{-1}=\boldsymbol{D}+(\boldsymbol{Z}_{\mathrm{hist}}-\boldsymbol{D}\boldsymbol{W}_{\mathrm{hist}})\boldsymbol{W}_{\mathrm{hist}}^{\dagger}$, where $\boldsymbol{Z}_{\mathrm{hist}}$ and $\boldsymbol{W}_{\mathrm{hist}}$ are paired response directions and approximate operator images from the preceding successful solve at the same k point, with $\boldsymbol{W}_{\mathrm{hist}}^{\dagger}\boldsymbol{W}_{\mathrm{hist}}\approx\boldsymbol{I}$. The images belong to the historical solve, not necessarily the current $\boldsymbol{L}$. Falls back to `kinetic` when no reliable history is available.
* `kinetic_subspace`: Apply $\boldsymbol{M}^{-1}=\boldsymbol{D}+(\boldsymbol{U}-\boldsymbol{D}\boldsymbol{L}\boldsymbol{U})(\boldsymbol{U}^{\dagger}\boldsymbol{L}\boldsymbol{U})^{-1}\boldsymbol{U}^{\dagger}$, where the columns of $\boldsymbol{U}$ are the previous-time wavefunctions defining the coarse subspace.
* `none`: Disable preconditioning.

Preconditioning changes the convergence rate, while `lin_thr` still controls the residual of the original equation.

lin_thr.description:
Nonnegative finite residual tolerance for each band in a PW real-time Crank-Nicolson solve $\boldsymbol{L}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$, with residual $\boldsymbol{r}=\boldsymbol{b}-\boldsymbol{L}\boldsymbol{x}$. A value of `0` selects $\tau=\max(10^{-10},100\epsilon)$, where $\epsilon$ is machine epsilon for the wavefunction precision. This gives a tolerance of approximately $1.19209\times10^{-5}$ in single precision and $10^{-10}$ in double precision. A positive value specifies $\tau$ directly.
* `bicgstab` and `gmres`: Require $\lVert\boldsymbol{r}\rVert\leqslant\tau\max(1,\lVert\boldsymbol{b}\rVert)$.
* `cgs`: Require $\lVert\boldsymbol{r}\rVert\leqslant\tau\lVert\boldsymbol{b}\rVert$ for nonzero $\boldsymbol{b}$, or $\lVert\boldsymbol{r}\rVert\leqslant\tau$ for zero $\boldsymbol{b}$.

All methods check the residual at the end of the linear solve, before orthonormalization. GMRES can use explicit residual reconstruction with periodic independent checks when `lin_reconstruct` is enabled. Subsequent orthonormalization uses a separate orthogonality tolerance and does not guarantee that the corrected wavefunctions satisfy the same linear residual tolerance.

lin_maxiter.description: Positive maximum number of iterations for each PW real-time linear solve. Failure to converge stops the calculation. Initial-state self-consistency uses `scf_nmax`; real-time self-consistency uses `td_scf_nmax`.

lin_gmres_restart.description: Positive maximum Arnoldi dimension per GMRES cycle. `lin_maxiter` limits the total iterations across all cycles.
lin_gmres_restart.availability: basis_type==pw and esolver_type==tddft and td_propagator==0 and lin_solver==gmres

td_cn_init.description: Project the Crank-Nicolson equation $\boldsymbol{L}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ onto the previous-time wavefunction subspace to initialize the first propagation solve of each time step. With those wavefunctions as the columns of $\boldsymbol{U}$, the projected initial guess is $\boldsymbol{x}_0=\boldsymbol{U}(\boldsymbol{U}^{\dagger}\boldsymbol{L}\boldsymbol{U})^{-1}\boldsymbol{U}^{\dagger}\boldsymbol{b}$. Evaluate and reuse the initial residual $\boldsymbol{r}_0=\boldsymbol{b}-\boldsymbol{L}\boldsymbol{x}_0$ using the stored subspace operator images $\boldsymbol{L}\boldsymbol{U}$, without an additional Hamiltonian application. Available with all linear solvers and preconditioners; later self-consistency iterations retain their current wavefunction guess.

lin_reconstruct.description:
Reconstruct the GMRES residual for $\boldsymbol{L}\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{b}$ as $\boldsymbol{r}=\boldsymbol{r}_0-(\boldsymbol{L}\boldsymbol{Z})\boldsymbol{y}$ for the update $\boldsymbol{x}=\boldsymbol{x}_0+\boldsymbol{Z}\boldsymbol{y}$, where $\boldsymbol{r}_0=\boldsymbol{b}-\boldsymbol{L}\boldsymbol{x}_0$ is the initial residual, $\boldsymbol{Z}$ contains the current preconditioned search directions, and $\boldsymbol{y}$ contains their update coefficients. Reusing the stored, unmodified operator images $\boldsymbol{L}\boldsymbol{Z}$ reduces Hamiltonian applications.

Use an internal tolerance of 0.8 times the effective `lin_thr` and independently verify the first solve at each k point and every 16 solves thereafter, with additional independent checks when needed. Failed reconstruction checks trigger a true-residual restart within `lin_maxiter`.

Only effective for `lin_solver=gmres`; ignored otherwise.
lin_reconstruct.availability: basis_type==pw and esolver_type==tddft and td_propagator==0 and lin_solver==gmres

estep_per_md.description: The number of electronic propagation steps between two ionic steps.

td_dt.description: The time step used for electronic propagation. If `td_dt` is not specified, it is set to `md_dt / estep_per_md`. If `td_dt` is specified explicitly, `md_dt` is reset to `td_dt * estep_per_md`.

td_edm.description:
Method used to calculate the energy-density matrix for the overlap contribution to forces in LCAO RT-TDDFT.
* `0`: Use $\mathrm{EDM}_{\boldsymbol{k}}=\frac{1}{2}\left(S_{\boldsymbol{k}}^{-1}H_{\boldsymbol{k}}\rho_{\boldsymbol{k}}+\rho_{\boldsymbol{k}}H_{\boldsymbol{k}}S_{\boldsymbol{k}}^{-1}\right)$.
* `1`: Use the ground-state eigenvalue-weighted expression $\mathrm{EDM}_{\mu\nu,\boldsymbol{k}}=\sum_i w_{i\boldsymbol{k}}\epsilon_{i\boldsymbol{k}}C_{\mu i,\boldsymbol{k}}C_{\nu i,\boldsymbol{k}}^*$. This expression is deprecated for RT-TDDFT and is generally not valid when the propagated wave functions are not Hamiltonian eigenstates.

td_print_eij.description:
Controls output of the propagated-state Hamiltonian matrix elements $E_{ij}=\Braket{\psi_i | \hat{H} | \psi_j}$ to the running log. The printed band indices $i$ and $j$ are global indices. Both the threshold and the printed matrix elements are in Ry.
* $\lt 0$: Disable the output.
* $\geqslant 0$: Print an element when either $\left|\operatorname{Re}E_{ij}\right|$ or $\left|\operatorname{Im}E_{ij}\right|$ is greater than or equal to `td_print_eij`.

td_propagator.description:
Method used to propagate the electronic states. The formulas below use Hartree atomic units, with $\Delta t$ denoting the electronic propagation time step and $S$ the LCAO overlap matrix. The Hamiltonian $H$ and overlap matrix $S$ are evaluated as required by each approximation.

For a plane-wave (PW) basis:
* `0`: Crank-Nicolson, $\left[I+\mathrm{i}H\Delta t/2\right]\psi(t+\Delta t)=\left[I-\mathrm{i}H\Delta t/2\right]\psi(t)$. The linear system uses the same midpoint Hamiltonian on both sides.
* `2`: Enforced time-reversal symmetry (ETRS), $U(t+\Delta t,t)=\exp\left[-\mathrm{i}H(t+\Delta t)\Delta t/2\right]\exp\left[-\mathrm{i}H(t)\Delta t/2\right]$. Select the exponential algorithm with `td_exp_method`.

For a nonorthogonal LCAO basis:
* `0`: Crank-Nicolson, $U=\left[S+\mathrm{i}H\Delta t/2\right]^{-1}\left[S-\mathrm{i}H\Delta t/2\right]$. The evolution matrix is constructed explicitly and applied to the wavefunctions.
* `1`: Fourth-order Taylor approximation to the exponential. With $\mathcal{A}=-\mathrm{i}S^{-1}H\Delta t$, $U=I+\mathcal{A}+\mathcal{A}^2/2+\mathcal{A}^3/6+\mathcal{A}^4/24$.
* `2`: Enforced time-reversal symmetry (ETRS), $U(t+\Delta t,t)=\exp\left[-\mathrm{i}S^{-1}H(t+\Delta t)\Delta t/2\right]\exp\left[-\mathrm{i}S^{-1}H(t)\Delta t/2\right]$. Each exponential uses the fourth-order Taylor approximation from method `1` with a half time step.
* `3`: Crank-Nicolson, $\left[S+\mathrm{i}H\Delta t/2\right]\psi(t+\Delta t)=\left[S-\mathrm{i}H\Delta t/2\right]\psi(t)$. The linear system is solved directly.

[NOTE] PW supports methods `0` and `2` on CPU and GPU. LCAO supports methods `0` through `3` on CPU and only method `0` on GPU.
td_propagator.requirements: When basis_type==pw and esolver_type==tddft: require td_propagator in [0, 2]

td_exp_method.description:
Algorithm used to evaluate $\exp(-\mathrm{i}\tau\boldsymbol{H})\boldsymbol{\psi}$ for Enforced time-reversal symmetry (ETRS) propagation with a plane-wave basis. The Hamiltonian $\boldsymbol{H}$ is held fixed over the evolution interval $\tau$. The formulas below use Hartree atomic units.
* `lanczos`: Adaptive Lanczos approximation with automatic reorthogonalization when needed. The estimated error relative to the input wavefunction norm is controlled by `td_exp_thr`, and the maximum Krylov dimension by `td_exp_krylov_dim`. The half-step and full-step predictor share a Krylov basis. If the error target cannot be met within the maximum dimension, the frozen-Hamiltonian interval is subdivided internally.
* `taylor`: Fixed-order Taylor approximation, $\exp(-\mathrm{i}\tau\boldsymbol{H})\boldsymbol{\psi}\approx\sum_{k=0}^{p}(-\mathrm{i}\tau\boldsymbol{H})^k\boldsymbol{\psi}/k!$, where the order $p$ is specified by `td_exp_order`.

td_exp_order.description: Taylor polynomial order $p$ used by `td_exp_method=taylor`. Must be an integer of at least 2.
td_exp_order.availability: basis_type==pw and esolver_type==tddft and td_propagator==2 and td_exp_method==taylor

td_exp_thr.description: Target for the estimated error in each Lanczos exponential calculation, relative to the input wavefunction norm. Must be nonnegative and finite. Zero selects $\max(10^{-10},100\epsilon)$, where $\epsilon$ is machine epsilon for the wavefunction precision, giving `1e-10` in double precision and approximately `1.19209e-5` in single precision. A positive value specifies the target directly.
td_exp_thr.availability: basis_type==pw and esolver_type==tddft and td_propagator==2 and td_exp_method==lanczos

td_exp_krylov_dim.description: Maximum number of Krylov basis vectors used in each Lanczos exponential calculation. Must be an integer of at least 2. Larger values increase wavefunction storage and orthogonalization work.
td_exp_krylov_dim.availability: basis_type==pw and esolver_type==tddft and td_propagator==2 and td_exp_method==lanczos

td_vext.description:
Controls the analytic time-dependent electric field. With `init_vecpot=True`, the external field is supplied through the vector-potential file instead, independently of `td_vext`.
* `True`: Enable the analytic electric field.
* `False`: Disable the analytic electric field.

td_vext_dire.description:
Specifies one absolute Cartesian direction for each external electric field when `td_vext` is enabled. Unlike the ground-state `efield_dir` parameter, these directions are not defined by lattice or reciprocal-lattice vectors. The number of values must equal that of `td_ttype`, and repeated directions are allowed; fields assigned to the same direction are added. For example, `td_vext_dire 1 2` applies one field along Cartesian x and one along Cartesian y.
* `1`: The external field direction is along the x-axis.
* `2`: The external field direction is along the y-axis.
* `3`: The external field direction is along the z-axis.

td_stype.description:
Type of electric field in the space domain, i.e. the gauge of the electric field.
* `0`: Length gauge, available for PW and LCAO.
* `1`: Velocity gauge, available for PW and LCAO.
* `2`: Hybrid gauge, available only for LCAO. See J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2025, 21, 3335-3341 for more information.

td_ttype.description:
Specifies one time-domain type for each external electric field. Its number of values must equal that of `td_vext_dire`. Parameters belonging to each type must provide exactly one value for every occurrence of that type, in occurrence order; fields with a repeated direction are added.

The formulas below use Hartree atomic units. For every ordinary input frequency $f$, $\omega=2\pi f$; $\Delta t=\mathtt{td\_dt}$; and $E_0$ denotes the corresponding amplitude parameter. A step-valued parameter $n_q$ represents the physical time $t_q=n_q\Delta t$.
* `0`: Gaussian pulse, $E(t)=E_0\cos\left[\omega(t-t_0)+\varphi\right]\mathrm{e}^{-(t-t_0)^2/(2\sigma^2)}$, where $t_0=\mathtt{td\_gauss\_t0}\Delta t$.
* `1`: Trapezoid pulse, $E(t)=E_0g(t)\cos(\omega t+\varphi)$. With $t_1=\mathtt{td\_trape\_t1}\Delta t$, $t_2=\mathtt{td\_trape\_t2}\Delta t$, and $t_3=\mathtt{td\_trape\_t3}\Delta t$, the envelope is $g(t)=t/t_1$ for $0\leqslant t\lt t_1$, $g(t)=1$ for $t_1\leqslant t\lt t_2$, $g(t)=(t_3-t)/(t_3-t_2)$ for $t_2\leqslant t\lt t_3$, and $g(t)=0$ otherwise.
* `2`: Trigonometric pulse, $E(t)=E_0\cos(\omega_1t+\varphi_1)\sin^2(\omega_2t+\varphi_2)$.
* `3`: Heaviside pulse defined on electronic steps. With $n_0=\mathtt{td\_heavi\_t0}$, $E(n)=E_0$ for $n\lt n_0$ and $E(n)=0$ for $n\geqslant n_0$.
* `4`: Finite-support supersine pulse. For $t_{\mathrm{s}}\lt t\lt t_{\mathrm{e}}$, the envelope is $f(t)=\left\{\sin\left[\pi\frac{t-t_{\mathrm{s}}}{t_{\mathrm{e}}-t_{\mathrm{s}}}\right]\right\}^{\frac{\pi}{\sigma}\left|\frac{t-t_{\mathrm{s}}}{t_{\mathrm{e}}-t_{\mathrm{s}}}-\frac{1}{2}\right|}$ and the electric field is $E(t)=E_0\left\{f(t)\cos\left[\omega\left(t-\frac{t_{\mathrm{s}}+t_{\mathrm{e}}}{2}\right)+\varphi\right]+\frac{\dot{f}(t)}{\omega}\sin\left[\omega\left(t-\frac{t_{\mathrm{s}}+t_{\mathrm{e}}}{2}\right)+\varphi\right]\right\}$. The corresponding analytic vector potential is $\boldsymbol{A}(t)=-\frac{E_0}{\omega}f(t)\sin\left[\omega\left(t-\frac{t_{\mathrm{s}}+t_{\mathrm{e}}}{2}\right)+\varphi\right]\hat{\boldsymbol{e}}$, with $\boldsymbol{E}(t)=-\partial\boldsymbol{A}(t)/\partial t$. The envelope, electric field, and vector potential are zero at the pulse boundaries and outside the interval.

In the velocity and hybrid gauges, ABACUS obtains the vector potential actually used in propagation by Simpson integration of the selected electric fields, including the supersine field, so a residual at the numerical-quadrature accuracy scale may remain.

td_tstart.description: First active electronic-step index of the analytic electric field. Index $n$ corresponds to time $n\Delta t$, where $\Delta t=\mathtt{td\_dt}$. The interval from `td_tstart` through `td_tend` includes both endpoints. In velocity and hybrid gauges, each active index $n$ selects the integration interval $[n\Delta t,(n+1)\Delta t]$; its result is used at the next endpoint. The initial state at time zero does not integrate a future interval. Ignored when `init_vecpot=True`.

td_tend.description: Last active electronic-step index of the analytic electric field, using the time convention defined by `td_tstart`. The interval includes both endpoints. In velocity and hybrid gauges, the last selected integration interval is $[\mathtt{td\_tend}\Delta t,(\mathtt{td\_tend}+1)\Delta t]$. Ignored when `init_vecpot=True`.

td_lcut1.description: Lower fractional-coordinate cutoff for the periodic spatial modulation used in the length gauge. Let $c_1=\mathtt{td\_lcut1}$, $c_2=\mathtt{td\_lcut2}$, $D=c_2-c_1$, and $G=c_1+1-c_2$. For a fractional coordinate $x$, the field factor is $\eta(x)=1$ when $c_1\leqslant x\lt c_2$ and $\eta(x)=-D/G$ elsewhere. The reversed outer interval makes the potential periodic and continuous and gives the field zero cell average.

td_lcut2.description: Upper fractional-coordinate cutoff for the periodic spatial modulation used in the length gauge. Let $c_1=\mathtt{td\_lcut1}$, $c_2=\mathtt{td\_lcut2}$, $D=c_2-c_1$, and $G=c_1+1-c_2$. For a fractional coordinate $x$, the field factor is $\eta(x)=1$ when $c_1\leqslant x\lt c_2$ and $\eta(x)=-D/G$ elsewhere. The reversed outer interval makes the potential periodic and continuous and gives the field zero cell average.

td_gauss_freq.description: Ordinary frequency $f$ in the Gaussian-pulse formula, with $\omega=2\pi f$. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 0` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_gauss_phase.description: Carrier phase $\varphi$ in the Gaussian-pulse formula. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 0` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_gauss_sigma.description: Nonzero standard deviation $\sigma$ of the Gaussian envelope. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 0` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_gauss_t0.description: Electronic-step position of the Gaussian center, which defines $t_0=\mathtt{td\_gauss\_t0}\Delta t$. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 0` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_gauss_amp.description: Electric-field scale $E_0$ in the Gaussian-pulse formula. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 0` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_trape_freq.description: Ordinary carrier frequency $f$ in the trapezoid-pulse formula, with $\omega=2\pi f$. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 1` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_trape_phase.description: Carrier phase $\varphi$ in the trapezoid-pulse formula. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 1` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_trape_t1.description: Electronic step defining the end of the linear rise, $t_1=\mathtt{td\_trape\_t1}\Delta t$. The value must be a nonnegative integer; integer-valued real inputs such as `2.0` are accepted. Each field must satisfy $\mathtt{td\_trape\_t1}\leqslant\mathtt{td\_trape\_t2}\leqslant\mathtt{td\_trape\_t3}$. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 1` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_trape_t2.description: Electronic step defining the end of the plateau, $t_2=\mathtt{td\_trape\_t2}\Delta t$. The value must be a nonnegative integer; integer-valued real inputs such as `2.0` are accepted. Each field must satisfy $\mathtt{td\_trape\_t1}\leqslant\mathtt{td\_trape\_t2}\leqslant\mathtt{td\_trape\_t3}$. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 1` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_trape_t3.description: Electronic step defining the end of the linear fall, $t_3=\mathtt{td\_trape\_t3}\Delta t$. The value must be a nonnegative integer; integer-valued real inputs such as `2.0` are accepted. Each field must satisfy $\mathtt{td\_trape\_t1}\leqslant\mathtt{td\_trape\_t2}\leqslant\mathtt{td\_trape\_t3}$. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 1` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_trape_amp.description: Electric-field scale $E_0$ in the trapezoid-pulse formula. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 1` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_trigo_freq1.description: First ordinary frequency $f_1$ in the trigonometric-pulse formula, with $\omega_1=2\pi f_1$. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 2` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_trigo_freq2.description: Second ordinary frequency $f_2$ in the trigonometric-pulse formula, with $\omega_2=2\pi f_2$. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 2` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_trigo_phase1.description: Carrier phase $\varphi_1$ in the cosine factor of the trigonometric-pulse formula. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 2` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_trigo_phase2.description: Envelope phase $\varphi_2$ in the sine-squared factor of the trigonometric-pulse formula. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 2` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_trigo_amp.description: Electric-field scale $E_0$ in the trigonometric-pulse formula. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 2` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_heavi_t0.description: Electronic switch step $n_0$ in the Heaviside-pulse definition. The field is $E_0$ for $n\lt n_0$ and zero for $n\geqslant n_0$. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 3` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_heavi_amp.description: Electric-field scale $E_0$ in the Heaviside-pulse definition. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 3` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_supsine_amp.description: Carrier electric-field scale $E_0$ of each supersine pulse. This is not a normalization of the complete waveform maximum, because the envelope-derivative term also contributes. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 4` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_supsine_freq.description: Nonzero ordinary carrier frequency $f$ of each supersine pulse, with $\omega=2\pi f$. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 4` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_supsine_phase.description: Electric-field carrier phase $\varphi$ at the center of each supersine envelope. A value of `0` places a cosine carrier maximum at the envelope center. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 4` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_supsine_sigma.description: Dimensionless shape parameter $\sigma$ of each supersine envelope. It must satisfy $0\lt\sigma\lt\pi/2$ so that the electric field approaches zero at the pulse boundaries. Supply exactly one value for each `td_ttype 4` occurrence, in occurrence order.

td_supsine_tstart.description: Integer electronic step at the left, exactly zero boundary of each supersine pulse, defining $t_{\mathrm{s}}=\mathtt{td\_supsine\_tstart}\Delta t$. Supply exactly one integer or `default` token for each `td_ttype 4` occurrence, in occurrence order; each `default` token inherits `td_tstart`. The complete pulse support must lie inside the inclusive global `td_tstart` to `td_tend` interval; hard truncation of a supersine pulse is rejected.

td_supsine_tend.description: Integer electronic step at the right, exactly zero boundary of each supersine pulse, defining $t_{\mathrm{e}}=\mathtt{td\_supsine\_tend}\Delta t$. Supply exactly one integer or `default` token for each `td_ttype 4` occurrence, in occurrence order; each `default` token inherits `td_tend`. The complete pulse support must lie inside the inclusive global `td_tstart` to `td_tend` interval; hard truncation of a supersine pulse is rejected.

init_vecpot.description:
Selects the source of the vector potential $\boldsymbol{A}$. The input file `vector_pot.txt` is read from the calculation working directory. Each non-comment line contains four columns: an integer label followed by $A_x$, $A_y$, and $A_z$ in Hartree atomic units. Rows are read in order; labels are not used for lookup. The first row corresponds to time zero, and subsequent rows are separated by `td_dt`. After the last row, $\boldsymbol{A}$ remains constant.

The file takes precedence over analytic waveforms, independently of `td_vext`, `td_tstart`, and `td_tend`.
* `True`: Read the vector potential from file.
* `False`: Obtain the vector potential from the configured analytic electric field.
init_vecpot.availability: esolver_type==tddft and ((basis_type==pw and td_stype==1) or (basis_type==lcao and td_stype in [1, 2]))
init_vecpot.requirements: When init_vecpot==true: require esolver_type==tddft and ((basis_type==pw and td_stype==1) or (basis_type==lcao and td_stype in [1, 2]))

ocp.description:
Controls fixed band occupations. In PW RT-TDDFT and calculations other than LCAO RT-TDDFT, fixed values from `ocp_set` are applied during electronic-state setup. PW real-time propagation preserves these initial occupations. In LCAO RT-TDDFT, the initial ground-state SCF determines occupations normally, and fixed values are applied during the subsequent real-time propagation steps.
* `True`: Use the fixed occupations specified by `ocp_set` at the stage described above.
* `False`: Determine occupations normally; real-time propagation preserves the initial SCF occupations.

ocp_set.description:
Fixed occupation weights used when `ocp` is `true`. Values are assigned in band order for each k-point, following k-point order. In PW RT-TDDFT and other calculations outside LCAO RT-TDDFT, this array is applied during electronic-state setup. PW propagation preserves these occupations. In LCAO RT-TDDFT, the initial ground-state SCF uses its normally determined occupations, and this array is applied only during subsequent real-time propagation steps. The repetition syntax `N*x` expands to `N` copies of `x`.
* Example: `1 10*1 0 1` expands to 13 values, with the 12th value equal to `0` and all other values equal to `1`.
* After expansion, provide one block of `nbands` values for each k-point. If `nspin` is `2`, provide all k-point blocks for spin up followed by all k-point blocks for spin down; otherwise, provide one block per k-point.
* The sum of all weights must equal `nelec`; otherwise the calculation terminates with an error.

of_cd.category: TDOFDFT: time dependent orbital free density functional theory
of_cd.description:
Added the current dependent(CD) potential. (https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.98.144302)
* True: Added the CD potential.
* False: Not added the CD potential.

of_mcd_alpha.category: TDOFDFT: time dependent orbital free density functional theory
of_mcd_alpha.description: The value of the parameter alpha in modified CD potential method. mCDPotential=alpha*CDPotential (proposed in paper PhysRevB.98.144302)

xc_kernel.description: The exchange-correlation kernel used in the calculation. Currently supported: RPA, LDA, PWLDA, PBE, and the hybrids HF, PBE0, HSE, B3LYP, CAM_PBEH, LC_PBE, LC_WPBE, LRC_WPBE, LRC_WPBEH. A hybrid kernel needs the ground state to use the same functional: the exact-exchange operator $[\alpha+\beta\,\mathrm{erfc}(\mu r)]/r$ is built from exx_fock_alpha ($\alpha$), exx_erfc_alpha ($\beta$) and exx_erfc_omega ($\mu$), which are keyed off dft_functional, not off this parameter.

lr_init_xc_kernel.description:
The method to initalize the xc kernel.
* "default": Calculate xc kernel from the ground-state charge density.
* "file": Read the xc kernel on grid from the provided files. The following words should be the paths of ".cube" files, where the first 1 (nspin==1) or 3 (nspin==2, namely spin-aa, spin-ab and spin-bb) will be read in. The parameter xc_kernel will be invalid. Now only LDA-type kernel is supported as the potential will be calculated by directly multiplying the transition density.
[NOTE] The "file" and "from_charge_file" modes support spectra only. Excited-state forces and relaxation require the consistent ground-state density and its response; externally supplied kernels or frozen densities do not provide these derivatives.
* "from_charge_file": Calculate fxc from the charge density read from the provided files. The following words should be the paths of ".cube" files, where the first nspin files will be read in.

lr_solver.description:
The method to solve the Casida equation in LR-TDDFT under Tamm-Dancoff approximation (TDA).
* dav/dav_subspace/cg: Construct and diagonalize the Hamiltonian matrix iteratively with Davidson/Non-ortho-Davidson/CG algorithm.
* lapack: Construct the full matrix and directly diagonalize with LAPACK.
* spectrum: Calculate absorption spectrum only without solving Casida equation.

lr_thr.description: The convergence threshold of iterative diagonalization solver for LR-TDDFT. It is a pure-math number with the same meaning as pw_diag_thr, but since the Casida equation is a one-shot eigenvalue problem, it is also the convergence threshold of LR-TDDFT.

nocc.description:
The number of occupied orbitals (up to HOMO) retained in the majority-spin LR-TDDFT window. A positive value selects a shared core prefix to discard from both spin channels; it does not change the ground-state occupations.
* If omitted, non-positive, or larger than the occupied majority-spin channel, all occupied orbitals are used.
* The full occupied window is determined by the effective electron number (including nelec_delta once) and the ground-state spin populations. For nspin=2, the minority-spin window has abs(N_up-N_down) fewer occupied orbitals.

[NOTE] For reliable excited-state forces and relaxation, retain all occupied orbitals. With a truncated occupied or virtual X window, the current analytic force is an approximation and may differ from finite differences of the selected truncated excitation energy. Zero-padding X into a larger Z virtual space is retained, but does not restore every active/inactive orbital-response term. Check force/window convergence.

nvirt.description:
The number of virtual orbitals (starting from LUMO) used in the LR-TDDFT calculation.

[NOTE] For reliable excited-state forces and relaxation, use all occupied orbitals, nbands = NLOCAL (the AO basis size), and the full spin-resolved virtual window, nvirt = nbands - nocc. Merely setting nvirt = nbands - nocc is insufficient when nbands < NLOCAL. The Z virtual window is widened to the available ground-state bands and X is zero-padded without changing the selected excitation energy; this does not make the force an exact derivative of a truncated-X problem. Changing nvirt itself generally changes the excitation energies. Truncated-window forces remain available with a warning and require convergence checks, especially before optimization.

lr_nstates.description: The number of 2-particle states to be solved.

lr_target_state.description:
Initial excited-state index for `calculation = relax`, counted from 0 within the spin channel selected by `lr_target_spin`.

The gradient of the followed state (or its degenerate multiplet selected by `lr_degen_mode`) is computed, since solving the Z-vector equation dominates the cost of an excited-state gradient. It also selects the state whose excitation energy is added to the ground-state total energy, which is the quantity the energy-based relaxation algorithms (`cg`, `bfgs`, `lbfgs`) line-search on.

Ignored outside `calculation = relax`: a single-point run solves and reports the gradients of every state.

[NOTE] This index seeds the first ionic step. Subsequent steps compute cross-geometry AO overlaps and transform them with the saved and current KS orbitals to compare excitation amplitudes in a common occupied/virtual basis. Orbital sign changes and rotations within those subspaces do not change the overlap criterion. Index changes and low overlaps are reported. In JT mode the selected normalized multiplet mixture and its orbital basis become the reference. The projection is not renormalized, so window leakage remains visible. Tracking currently requires a fixed cell and unchanged orbital windows; degeneracy and a state leaving the solved window still limit state identification. Increase `lr_nstates` or reduce the ionic step when the overlap is low.

lr_degen_thr.description:
Excited states whose excitation energies lie within this threshold of each other are treated as one degenerate multiplet, and the full gradient matrix $G^{(A\alpha)}_{kl}=\langle X_k|\partial A/\partial R_{A\alpha}|X_l\rangle$ is computed for it in addition to the per-state gradients. Zero (the default) disables this and leaves the per-state gradients as the only output.

At a $d$-fold degeneracy no single state has a gradient vector: the branch slopes along a displacement $u$ are the eigenvalues of $\sum_{A\alpha}u_{A\alpha}G^{(A\alpha)}$, and the eigenvectors that diagonalise it depend on $u$. The per-state gradients are the diagonal of $G$ in whichever basis the eigensolver happened to return, so only their sum (the trace) is basis-independent, while $G$ itself is the complete first-order information -- it is the linear vibronic coupling Hamiltonian of the multiplet. The extra cost is $d(d-1)/2$ further Z-vector solves per multiplet.

The threshold proposes candidates; it cannot tell a true degeneracy from an accidental near-degeneracy, where the states have genuinely different excitation energies and the construction does not apply. Each multiplet's actual energy spread and the orthonormality of its eigenvectors are reported in the running log so the distinction can be made there.

[NOTE] In `lr_degen_mode = jt`, all members of a threshold-defined group are approximated as sharing one energy: relaxation reports their mean excitation energy but uses the selected JT mixed-state force. At an exact degeneracy this force gives the first-order branch slope; no additional mixing-coefficient response is required. With a finite energy spread below this threshold, however, the mean energy and JT force are generally not derivatives of the same surface. Energy-based line searches can therefore be inconsistent within this grouping interval, even if the spread is small. The ordinary single-root energy and force resume when the tracked group becomes a singleton after threshold-based splitting. This threshold does not bound the resulting force error. Check the reported spreads against numerical accuracy and test sensitivity to the grouping threshold before relying on JT relaxation convergence.

[NOTE] A sensible value is a few times the eigensolver threshold `lr_thr`, so that states split by real physics are not merged.

lr_degen_mode.description:
What `calculation = relax` follows when `lr_target_state` sits inside a degenerate multiplet, as identified by `lr_degen_thr`. It has no effect when the target state is non-degenerate.

* state: follow the gradient of that one state, as returned by the eigensolver. This is the historical behaviour and is what reproduces earlier results, but inside a multiplet it is not a well-defined quantity: the per-state gradients are the diagonal of the subspace gradient matrix in whichever basis the eigensolver happened to return, so they depend on numerical details of the diagonalisation rather than on physics.
* average: follow the multiplet average $\bar\Omega=\frac{1}{d}\sum_k\Omega_k$, whose gradient is $\operatorname{Tr}G/d$. For a fixed complete multiplet the average is basis-independent and its gradient respects the multiplet symmetry. Tracking allows groups to split or merge: split groups are not recombined to enforce symmetry, so changing group membership can change the average surface and lose geometric symmetry. Groups larger than three are tracked but use the selected single-state energy and force with a warning. Both the reported energy and the reported gradient switch to the average together, which the energy-based optimisers (`cg`, `bfgs`, `lbfgs`) require -- a gradient of one surface line-searched against the energy of another does not converge. This mode deliberately does NOT find the Jahn-Teller distortion, which is orthogonal to the totally symmetric average gradient.
* jt: descend the Jahn-Teller branch for a two- or three-state multiplet; larger JT force groups are rejected before gradient construction. Solves $\min_{\|u\|=1}\lambda_{\min}(\sum_{A\alpha}u_{A\alpha}G^{(A\alpha)})$ -- a joint optimisation over the displacement and the mixing inside the multiplet, since the two are determined together -- and follows the force of the resulting branch. This needs the off-diagonal part of the gradient matrix, so it costs $d(d-1)/2$ further Z-vector solves per step on top of the $d$ diagonal ones. The running log reports the branch's force, its mixing coefficients, and its split into the part common to the multiplet and the part that actually breaks the degeneracy.

[NOTE] Groups have no tracking dimension cap. `average` ranks groups by total cross-geometry subspace overlap; `jt` instead ranks by the projection weight of the previous actual JT mixture in each current group. The running log records both dimensions, coverage and singular values. Lost coverage is diagnosed and tracking continues; this does not guarantee a continuous energy surface. For `average`, ties use the previous selected-state projection weight; for `jt`, ties use total subspace overlap.

[NOTE] The usual sequence is `average` first, to reach the symmetric stationary point, then `jt` from there: at a stationary point of the average surface the common part vanishes and the whole force is Jahn-Teller. `jt` returns to the ordinary single-state energy and force once threshold-based splitting leaves the tracked group with one member; smaller splittings remain subject to the approximation described under `lr_degen_thr`.

[NOTE] `jt` gives the first-order DIRECTION. The distortion amplitude also needs the harmonic term, and the step norm is Cartesian rather than mass-weighted. A linear molecule has no first-order term at all (the effect is second-order Renner-Teller) and the log says so.

lr_grad_solver.description:
The method to solve the Z-vector (relaxed-density) equation $(A+B)Z=R$ in LR-TDDFT force and relaxation calculations, the linear-equation counterpart of `lr_solver`. Its dimension is $n_k n_{occ} n_{virt}$ summed over spin, where $n_{virt}$ counts every virtual band of the ground state, not only the `nvirt` window of the excitation.
* cg: Solve iteratively with the conjugate-gradient method, applying the orbital Hessian $A+B$ to a vector at each step. The matrix is never built.
* lapack: Construct the full matrix and solve directly with LAPACK (LU). Every MPI process holds the whole matrix and solves the same system.
* scalapack: Construct the matrix distributed over the MPI processes (2D block-cyclic) and solve with ScaLAPACK (LU).
* scalapack_chol: Construct the matrix distributed as for scalapack and solve by a ScaLAPACK Cholesky factorization, about half the flops of the LU and in place.

[NOTE] The direct solvers build the matrix column by column, at the cost of one application of $A+B$ per column, which usually dominates the cost of the solve itself; scalapack and scalapack_chol need an MPI build.

[NOTE] scalapack_chol requires $A+B$ to be positive definite. A non-positive-definite matrix causes an error on every MPI rank; use lr_grad_solver=scalapack (LU) instead. The LU solver does not require positive definiteness, but still requires a nonsingular matrix. The former elpa option has been removed; use scalapack_chol for distributed Cholesky.

lr_target_spin.description:
Which spin channel `lr_target_state` indexes.

* singlet / triplet: the two closed-shell channels solved at `nspin = 2`. At `nspin = 1` only `singlet` exists.
* updown: the single spin-conserving channel of an open-shell calculation (`lr_unrestricted`, or a spin-polarised ground state with a non-zero moment).

An open-shell calculation has only one channel, so any value is accepted there and relaxes that channel; an explicit `triplet` is reported as ignored. A closed-shell calculation rejects `updown`, since singlet and triplet are separate states with separate gradients.

Ignored outside `calculation = relax`.

lr_unrestricted.description:
Whether to use unrestricted construction for LR-TDDFT (the matrix size will be doubled).
* True: Always use unrestricted LR-TDDFT.
* False: Use unrestricted LR-TDDFT only when the system is open-shell.

abs_wavelen_range.description: The range of the wavelength for the absorption spectrum calculation.

out_wfc_lr.description: Whether to output the eigenstates (excitation energy) and eigenvectors (excitation amplitude) of the LR-TDDFT calculation. The output files are OUT.{suffix}/Excitation_Amplitude_${processor_rank}.dat.

abs_gauge.description: Optical gauge for LR-TDDFT/BSE: length or velocity. Set none to skip transition dipoles, oscillator strengths, transition analysis and absorption spectra, while retaining excitation energies, requested charge output, and LR forces or relaxation.

abs_broadening.description: The broadening factor for the absorption spectrum calculation.

bse_tda.description: Whether the Tamm-Dancoff approximation is used: 'tda', 'full', or 'both'.

bse_spin_types.description: Spin types for a closed-shell calculation in one task: 'singlet', 'triplet', and the test modes 'rpa' and 'ipa'.

bse_mem_save.description: Whether to save memory by adding V and W directly to the BSE matrix. When enabled, bse_ri_hartree is enabled and bse_continue is reset to 0.

bse_ri_hartree.description: Whether to use the RI approximation for the Hartree term in BSE.

bse_use_fine_kgrid.description: Fine k-grid mode for BSE: 0 uses the coarse k-grid, 1 uses a uniform fine k-grid, and 2 uses a non-uniform fine k-grid. Modes 1 and 2 require band_kpath_info, band_KS_eigenvector_k_{index}.txt, KS_band_spin_{index}.txt, and GW_band_spin_{index}.txt.

bse_q_approx_mode.description: q-to-k-pair mapping mode for W: 0=exact, 1=coarse q grid, 2=mixed, 3=truncate pairs with |q|>threshold (W elements dropped)

bse_q_approx_threshold.description: Threshold radius in unit of 2*pi/lat0 (same unit system as kvec_c) for exact q-to-k-pair mapping when bse_q_approx_mode is 2; in mode 3 pairs with larger |q| are dropped entirely.

out_bse_ab.description: Whether to output the AB matrix to a file.

bse_continue.description: Step from which to continue a previous BSE calculation: 0 starts a new calculation; 1 reads A_V; 2 reads A_V and A_W; 3 reads A_V, A_W, and B_V; 4 reads A_V, A_W, B_V, and B_W.

plot_istate.description: The index of the excited state to plot, starting from 0.

exciton_plot_type.description: Exciton density represented when lr_solver is 'plot': 'average' integrates out the other particle, while 'conditional' fixes one particle at exciton_fixed_coordinate and plots a slice of the other particle's density.

exciton_plot_format.description: The exciton-density output format. Average density supports cube, slice, and both; conditional density supports slice only.

exciton_fixed_coordinate.description: Cartesian coordinates in Bohr used by conditional exciton plotting, in the order hole_x hole_y hole_z electron_x electron_y electron_z.

exciton_slice_plane.description: Pair of lattice-vector directions spanning the cross section: 'ab', 'bc', or 'ca'.

exciton_slice_pos.description: Offset in Bohr along the remaining lattice-vector direction: c for an ab slice, a for bc, and b for ca.

exciton_slice_npoints.description: Target in-plane grid resolution. The final grid uses a uniform number of points per primitive cell over `exciton_slice_range` and includes both endpoints.

exciton_slice_range.description: The in-plane primitive-cell range of an exciton slice: ustart uend vstart vend. The end values are exclusive cell boundaries, while grid data include both range endpoints.

dfpt_qmesh.description: Set the Monkhorst-Pack q mesh (gamma-centered) for DFPT phonon calculations. The q mesh must be commensurate with the ground-state k mesh: k + q must be a point of the k list (modulo a reciprocal lattice vector). For example, a 4x4x4 KPT mesh is commensurate with dfpt_qmesh values of 1, 2, or 4 along each direction. This parameter is ignored when dfpt_qfile is set.

dfpt_qfile.description: Set the file containing the q points for DFPT, in the same format as the KPT file (Q_POINTS card: Gamma/Monkhorst-Pack mesh, or an explicit Direct/Cartesian list; symmetry reduction is not applied to file q lists). When set, it overrides dfpt_qmesh. Each q point must still be commensurate with the ground-state k mesh. When dfpt_compute_q0 is true, Gamma must be the FIRST q point and must appear exactly once (the run rejects [X, Gamma] and [Gamma, X, Gamma] orderings at input time, regardless of dfpt_out_dyn); arbitrary orderings are allowed when dfpt_compute_q0 is false.

dfpt_compute_q0.description: Whether to compute the macroscopic dielectric tensor (epsilon_inf) and the Born effective charges at q = 0 within the same DFPT run. Requires Gamma as the FIRST q point, exactly once (the default dfpt_qmesh 1 1 1 satisfies this); orderings such as [X, Gamma] or [Gamma, X, Gamma] are rejected at input time, independently of dfpt_out_dyn.

dfpt_loto.description: Whether to apply the Lyddane-Sachs-Teller non-analytic correction to the Gamma-point dynamical matrix, which splits the longitudinal and transverse optical modes. Requires dfpt_compute_q0 to be true, since the correction is built from epsilon_inf and the Born effective charges.

dfpt_out_dyn.description: Write one QE-compatible dyn file per q point into the output directory: OUT.<suffix>/dyn.q<i>. Each file contains the unreduced (pre-ASR, pre-LO-TO) force-constant matrix Phi in Ry/bohr^2, the same content and layout as Quantum ESPRESSO's ph.x output (fildyn), so the files can be diffed element-by-element against QE references or post-processed by external tools. At Gamma with dfpt_compute_q0 the Born effective charges and dielectric tensor are appended in the QE convention.

dfpt_conv_thr.description: Set the convergence threshold of the self-consistent DFPT cycle: the iteration stops when the relative residual of the mixed variable drops below this value for every displacement. With dfpt_mix_type = v_sc_plain or v_sc_broyden (the default) the residual is the screening-potential residual ||v_out - v_in|| / ||v_out||; with rho_plain, rho_kerker or rho_broyden it is the first-order density residual ||drho_out - drho_in|| / ||drho_out||. The electric-field (LO-TO) solve always mixes the density, using the density-space counterpart of the selected scheme (e.g. rho_broyden when dfpt_mix_type = v_sc_broyden), so its residual is always the density residual.

dfpt_max_iter.description: Set the maximum number of self-consistent DFPT iterations for each atomic displacement.

dfpt_lin_conv_thr.description: Dedicated convergence threshold of the projected CG solve of the Sternheimer equation inside every DFPT response iteration, as the relative residual ||P_c r|| / ||P_c b|| of the projected system (r: CG residual, b: projected right-hand side, P_c: complement of the occupied subspace at k+q). Non-positive values (the default) inherit dfpt_conv_thr, which reproduces the historical single-knob behavior. Accuracy tradeoff of truncating the inner solve: the outer mixing residual does NOT check the achieved Sternheimer residual, so a loose inner threshold or a small dfpt_lin_max_iter can shift converged observables; the same controls also affect the one-shot Gamma position response (the bare q = 0 operator legs inherit them as well). When the knobs are tightened for a hard response, validate the phonons, dielectric tensor and Born charges against tighter inner settings to quantify the truncation error. Decouple them when a flat semicore band system needs a loose inner solve to keep the outer mixing stable: the shifted operator is then near-singular and a very deep inner solve amplifies the response beyond what the outer mixing can damp.

dfpt_lin_max_iter.description: Dedicated iteration cap of the projected CG solve of the Sternheimer equation inside every DFPT response iteration. Non-positive values (the default) inherit dfpt_max_iter, which reproduces the historical single-knob behavior. Lower it to truncate the CG before it drives into near-singular directions of a flat-band system; raise it for otherwise unconverged inner solves without enlarging the outer mixing budget. The cap has the same accuracy tradeoff as dfpt_lin_conv_thr: the outer mixing residual does not check the achieved Sternheimer residual, the one-shot Gamma position response shares the cap, and truncated inner solves should be validated against tighter settings on the phonons, dielectric tensor and Born charges.

dfpt_mix_beta.description: Set the plain-mixing coefficient of the DFPT response SCF. It scales the preliminary step of the chosen dfpt_mix_type (the plain mix itself, or the initial guess pushed into the Broyden history). The response Jacobian has strongly negative eigenvalues on the smallest-G shells (Coulomb stiffness), so beta must stay below 2 / (1 + |lambda_min|); the default 0.4 keeps margin up to |lambda_min| ~ 3. A larger value accelerates convergence for weakly screened systems but may diverge.

dfpt_asr.description: Enforce the translational acoustic sum rule (sum over atoms of the Gamma force-constant rows = 0) on the RAW Gamma dynamical matrix, before the LO-TO nonanalytic term, together with the Z* sum rule sum_a Z*_a = 0 on the Born effective charges. Unconstrained linear-response self-consistency violates both at the percent to tens-of-percent level (QE ph.x shows the same), and the reference workflow post-processes with asr='crystal'. simple: subtract each row sum from its diagonal element. crystal: the optimized minimal-norm symmetric projection (keeps Hermiticity and symmetry-equivalent atoms equivalent). no: leave the matrix as computed.

dfpt_mix_type.description: Set the mixing scheme of the DFPT response SCF. rho_plain: the first-order density is mixed with the same coefficient dfpt_mix_beta on every shell. rho_kerker: the Kerker screen f_g = |G+q|^2 / (|G+q|^2 + a^2) damps the Coulomb-stiff smallest shells, stabilizing polar / small-gap systems at beta up to 1; a^2 is set by dfpt_kerker_a2. rho_broyden: Modified Broyden mixing (Johnson 1988) on the density, history depth dfpt_broyden_ndim. v_sc_plain / v_sc_broyden: mix the screening potential v_sc = v_H[drho] + v_xc[drho] instead of the density, with plain or Modified Broyden coefficients; v_sc_broyden is the default (the metric the Broyden least squares works in is K-weighted, which stabilizes the Coulomb-stiff shells that destabilize plain density mixing).

dfpt_kerker_a2.description: Set the Kerker screening parameter a^2 (in 1/lat0^2 units) used by dfpt_mix_type = rho_kerker. The screen f_g = |G+q|^2 / (|G+q|^2 + a^2) freezes the stiff long-wavelength shells; larger a^2 damps more shells. Ignored by the other schemes.

dfpt_broyden_ndim.description: Set the number of history steps used by the Modified Broyden mixing (Johnson 1988) when dfpt_mix_type = rho_broyden or v_sc_broyden. Under v_sc_broyden it sizes both Broyden instances: the screening-potential mixer of the displacement loop and the density mixer of the electric-field (LO-TO) loop. More history generally accelerates convergence at the cost of memory.

out_freq_ion.description:
Controls the output interval in ionic steps. When set to a positive integer, information such as charge density, local potential, electrostatic potential, Hamiltonian matrix, overlap matrix, density matrix, Mulliken population analysis, and structure files (STRU{istep} or STRU{istep}.cif, when out_stru is 1 or 2) is printed every n ionic steps.

This parameter only controls how often a write happens, not how many files are kept: with out_app_flag = 0 each write overwrites the same fixed filename, with out_app_flag = 1 records are appended to one fixed filename, and with out_app_flag = 2 each written step gets its own g{step} file.

In molecular dynamics calculations, out_freq_ion controls the cadence of the structure frames written when out_stru is positive; when out_freq_ion is 0, md_restartfreq is used as the structure-output frequency. The MD restart file Restart_md.txt always follows md_restartfreq and is independent of out_freq_ion.

For DFT+U calculations with out_occ_mat = 1, a separate occupation-matrix file occ_matg{geom_step}.txt is created for every output ionic step. The converged (or final, if not converged) electronic step is always recorded in that file; when out_freq_elec is set smaller than scf_nmax, additional electronic steps are appended as separate sections, each labelled only with the electronic-step number.

[NOTE] In RT-TDDFT calculations, this parameter is inactive; output frequency is instead controlled by out_freq_td.

out_freq_td.description:
Controls the output interval in completed electronic evolution steps during RT-TDDFT calculations. When set to a positive integer `n`, detailed information (see `out_freq_ion`) is printed every `n` electron time-evolution steps (i.e., every `STEP OF ELECTRON EVOLVE`). For example, if you wish to output information once per ionic step, you should set `out_freq_td` equal to `estep_per_md`, since one ionic step corresponds to `estep_per_md` electronic evolution steps.

[NOTE] This parameter is only active in RT-TDDFT mode (`esolver_type = tddft`). It has no effect in ground-state calculations.

out_freq_elec.description:
Output the charge density (only binary format, controlled by out_chg), wavefunction (controlled by out_wfc_pw) per out_freq_elec electronic iterations. Note that they are always output when converged or reach the maximum iterations scf_nmax.

In DFT+U calculations with out_freq_ion > 0 and out_occ_mat = 1, this parameter also selects the electronic iterations recorded as separate sections inside occ_matg{geom_step}.txt (the converged or final electronic step is recorded regardless of this parameter).

out_occ_mat.description:
Whether to output the DFT+U occupation matrices. When set to 1 (default), the latest occupation matrix is written to occ_mat.txt at every electronic step, and a numbered file occ_matg{geom_step}.txt is created for every output ionic step selected by out_freq_ion, in which electronic-step sections are appended according to out_freq_elec. Sorted eigenvalues of the stored occupation matrix are appended as comment lines only to the latest occ_mat.txt, not to the numbered files. For nspin=1, one nonmagnetic spectrum is written.

This parameter only takes effect for DFT+U calculations (dft_plus_u > 0) and is independent of out_chg: disabling the charge density output does not disable the occupation-matrix output.

out_sol.description:
* 0: No output.
* 1: Output the implicit-solvent fields of the last solvent correction on real space grids into files in the folder OUT.{suffix}, for imp_sol 1 (the original implicit solvation model) and imp_sol 2 (SCCS):
 * `sol_eps.cube`: the dielectric function epsilon(r), 1 in the solute and the bulk permittivity in the solvent.
 * `sol_cavity.cube`: the solute boundary s(r), 1 in the solute and 0 in the solvent; for imp_sol 1 it is 1 minus the solvent shape function (written only when eb_k > 1). With the solvent-aware cavity (sccs_solvent_radius > 0) it is the filled boundary.
 * `sol_cavity_local.cube` and `sol_filled_fraction.cube`: only with the solvent-aware cavity, the boundary before the filling and the solute fraction of the probe sphere around each point; points where this fraction exceeds sccs_filling_thr are filled.
 With out_freq_ion > 0 the files are written every out_freq_ion ionic steps; with out_freq_ion = 0 they are written at every step. In out_app_flag 1, fixed names such as `sol_eps.cube` hold one complete frame per written step: ionic step 0 truncates the file and later steps append. In out_app_flag 2, positive out_freq_ion adds the geometry index, e.g. `sol_epsg1.cube`. In mode 0, and in mode 2 with out_freq_ion = 0, each written step overwrites the fixed name. Solvent files stay in OUT.{suffix} in all modes. Nothing is written while SCCS waits for its delayed start (sccs_start_drho).

The optional second integer controls the output precision. If not provided, the default precision is 8.

out_dmk.description:
Whether to output the density matrix for each k-point into files in the folder OUT.${suffix}. For current develop versions, out_dmk writes *_nao.txt files:
    * For gamma only case:
     * nspin = 1 and 4: dm_nao.txt;
     * nspin = 2: dms1_nao.txt and dms2_nao.txt for the two spin channels.
    * For multi-k points case:
     * nspin = 1 and 4: dmk1_nao.txt, dmk2_nao.txt, ...;
     * nspin = 2: dmk1s1_nao.txt... and dmk1s2_nao.txt... for the two spin channels.

    The file names are fixed for out_app_flag = 0 (overwritten at every write) and out_app_flag = 1 (records appended). Only out_app_flag = 2 inserts a one-based geometry-step suffix before _nao (for example dmk1g1_nao.txt).

    [NOTE] Version difference (develop vs 3.10-LTS):
    * In develop, out_dmk supports both gamma-only and multi-k-point density-matrix output.
    * In 3.10-LTS, the corresponding keyword is out_dm, and the output files are SPIN1_DM and SPIN2_DM, etc.

out_dmr.description:
Whether to output the density matrix with Bravias lattice vector R index into files in the folder OUT.${suffix}. The files are named as dmr{s}{spin index}{g}{geometry index}{_nao} + {".csr"}. Here, 's' refers to spin, where s1 means spin up channel while s2 means spin down channel, and the sparse matrix format 'csr' is mentioned in out_hsr. Finally, the file name is fixed for out_app_flag = 0 (truncated and overwritten at every write) and out_app_flag = 1 (the first written step truncates it and later steps append complete records); only out_app_flag = 2 inserts a one-based geometry-step index for each ionic step that may have different geometries:
* nspin = 1: dmrs1_nao.csr;
* nspin = 2: dmrs1_nao.csr and dmrs2_nao.csr for the two spin channels.

[NOTE] In the 3.10-LTS version, the parameter is named out_dm1, and the file names are data-DMR-sparse_SPIN0.csr and data-DMR-sparse_SPIN1.csr, etc.

out_wfc_pw.description:
Controls whether plane-wave Kohn-Sham wavefunction coefficients are written to `OUT.${suffix}/`.

Available values are:
* `0`: Do not write wavefunction coefficients.
* `1`: Write text files with the `.txt` suffix.
* `2`: Write binary files with the `.dat` suffix.

The file-name pattern is `wfk{k}[s{spin}][g{geometry step}][e{electronic iteration}]_pw.txt` for `out_wfc_pw=1` and `wfk{k}[s{spin}][g{geometry step}][e{electronic iteration}]_pw.dat` for `out_wfc_pw=2`. All PW output files include a `k*` label, including Gamma-only calculations. Without geometry-step or electronic-iteration indices, representative names are `wfk1_pw.txt` or `wfk1_pw.dat` for `nspin=1`, `wfk1s1_pw.txt` and `wfk1s2_pw.txt` or their `.dat` equivalents for `nspin=2`, and `wfk1s4_pw.txt` or `wfk1s4_pw.dat` for `nspin=4`.

With `out_freq_ion=0`, files are written only when the electronic calculation converges or reaches `scf_nmax`; no `g*` or `e*` index is added. During structural relaxation or molecular dynamics with `out_app_flag=1`, the first written step truncates the unindexed files and later ionic steps append one frame per step (mirroring `out_wfc_lcao`); with `out_app_flag=0` the unindexed files are overwritten each step. With `out_freq_ion` > 0, output is restricted to the ionic steps selected by `out_freq_ion`. For `out_app_flag=0` or `2`, output is written when the electronic iteration is a multiple of `out_freq_elec`, when the calculation converges, or when it reaches `scf_nmax`; for `out_app_flag=1` only the last electronic iteration of each selected ionic step is written (out_freq_elec is ignored), so the appended file holds exactly one frame per step. Both `g*` and `e*` indices are then added only when `out_app_flag=2`; with `out_app_flag=0` the fixed files are truncated and overwritten at every write, and with `out_app_flag=1` they accumulate one frame per written step.

With `init_wfc file binary`, ABACUS reads only unindexed binary `wf*_pw.dat` files from `read_file_dir`, starting from the first frame. Such directly reusable files are normally generated with `out_wfc_pw=2` and `out_freq_ion=0`; multi-frame files accumulated under `out_app_flag=1` are trajectories and only their first frame is visible to the reader. Text `wf*_pw.txt` files and files containing `g*` or `e*` indices are not matched automatically.

[NOTE] In the 3.10-LTS version, the binary files are named `WAVEFUNC1.dat`, `WAVEFUNC2.dat`, etc.

out_wfc_lcao.description:
Whether to output the electronic wavefunction coefficients into files and store them in the folder OUT.${suffix} (or its PSI/ subdirectory when out_app_flag is 2). The files are named as wf{s}{spin index}{k(optional)}{k-point index}{g(optional)}{geometry index1}{_nao} + {".txt"/".dat"}. Here, 's' refers to spin, where s1 means spin up channel while s2 means spin down channel, and 's12' refer to spinor wave functions that contains both spin channels with spin-orbital coupling or noncollinear calculations enabled. In addition, if 'gamma_only' is set to 0, then the optinoal k-point sampling index appears with the k-point index attached to the electronic wave function file names. Finally, only out_app_flag = 2 adds the optional 'g' index for each ionic step that may have different geometries, and the wave function files are saved into the PSI/ subdirectory of OUT.${suffix}; with out_app_flag = 0 the fixed file is truncated and overwritten at every write, and with out_app_flag = 1 the wave functions accumulate during ionic steps.
* 0: no output
* 1: (txt format)
 * gamma-only: wfs1_nao.txt or wfs2_nao.txt, ...;
 * non-gamma-only: wfs1k1_nao.txt or wfs1k2_nao.txt, ...;
* 2: (binary format)
 * gamma-only: wfs1_nao.dat or wfs2_nao.dat, ...;
 * non-gamma-only: wfs1k1_nao.dat or wfs1k2_nao.dat, ....

The corresponding sequence of the orbitals can be seen in Basis Set.

Also controled by out_freq_ion and out_app_flag.

[NOTE] In the 3.10-LTS version, the file names are WFC_NAO_GAMMA1_ION1.txt and WFC_NAO_K1_ION1.txt, etc.

out_dos.description:
Whether to output the density of states (DOS) and projected density of states (PDOS). For more information, refer to the dos.md.
* 0: no output
* 1: output the density of states (DOS) and projected density of states (PDOS, LCAO only)
 * With out_app_flag = 0: fixed-name files (`doss{s}.txt`, `pdoss{s}.txt`) are truncated and overwritten at every write.
 * With out_app_flag = 1: the same fixed-name files are reused; the first written step truncates them and later steps append one record per step (prefixed with a `# ionic step N` header, one-based).
 * With out_app_flag = 2: per-step files are named `doss{s}g{geom}.txt` and `pdoss{s}g{geom}.txt` where `{geom}` is the one-based geometry index (e.g. `doss1g3.txt` for the third ionic step).
 * nspin=1 or 4: one spin channel (`s1`). nspin=2: two channels (`s1`, `s2`). PW and LCAO use the same naming.
Note: values 2 and 3 are no longer supported. Setting out_dos to 2 or 3 will raise an error.

out_ldos.description:
Whether to output the local density of states (LDOS), optionally output precision can be set by a second parameter, default is 3.
* 0: no output
* 1: output the partial charge density for given bias (controlled by stm_bias) in cube file format, which can be used to plot scanning tunneling spectroscopys to mimick STM images using the Python script plot.py.
* 2: output LDOS along a line in real space (controlled by ldos_line). Parameters used to control DOS output are also valid for LDOS.
* 3: output both two LDOS modes above.

out_proj_band.description: Whether to output the projected band structure. For more information, refer to the band.md

out_stru.description:
Controls the output of structure files per ionic step. The files are written to the OUT.{suffix}/ directory (or the OUT.{suffix}/STRUC/ subdirectory when out_app_flag is 2). Each file corresponds to the structure at the current ionic step; in the relaxation path the header comment records the ABACUS version, timestamp, energy, and stress tensor, while MD frames written to a cumulative file are prefixed with a one-based "# MD step N" marker. When out_freq_ion is positive and out_app_flag is not 0, the numbered files STRU{istep} (or STRU{istep}.cif) are written every out_freq_ion steps; when out_freq_ion is 0 or out_app_flag is 0, no numbered files are output (with out_app_flag = 0 the latest structure is still kept in STRU_NOW / STRU_NOW.cif). This parameter is effective for scf/nscf/relax/cell-relax and md; for md only values 0 and 1 are supported, because MD structure frames are written in ABACUS STRU format and read back by the restart logic, so value 2 (CIF) is rejected. For scf/nscf only STRU_FINAL (or STRU_FINAL.cif) is written.
    - 0: No structure files are output.
    - 1: ABACUS STRU format files are output. In scf/nscf/relax/cell-relax the latest structure is written to STRU_NOW (overwritten each step), the numbered file STRU{istep} (e.g., STRU1, STRU2) is written every out_freq_ion steps (when out_freq_ion is positive), and the final converged structure is written to STRU_FINAL. No CIF files are output. When out_app_flag is 1, the numbered STRU{istep} files are replaced by a single fixed-name STRU file that appends one structure block (with a one-based "# Ionic Step N" or "# MD step N" comment) per written step.
    - 2: CIF format files are output. The latest structure is written to STRU_NOW.cif (overwritten each step), the numbered file STRU{istep}.cif (e.g., STRU1.cif, STRU2.cif) is written every out_freq_ion steps (when out_freq_ion is positive), and the final converged structure is written to STRU_FINAL.cif. No non-CIF files are output. When out_app_flag is 1, the numbered files are replaced by a fixed-name STRU.cif overwritten each written step. Not supported for calculation = md, which always writes ABACUS STRU frames.
[NOTE] MD structure output differs from the ionic-relaxation path: frames are written every out_freq_ion steps, falling back to md_restartfreq when out_freq_ion is 0; out_app_flag = 0 keeps the numbered STRU{istep} files (STRU1 is the initial geometry) and no STRU_NOW is written; out_app_flag = 2 writes the numbered files under STRUC/; out_app_flag = 1 writes one cumulative STRU file that is truncated on the first frame of a fresh run and appended with a "# MD step N" marker afterwards. MD never writes STRU_NOW or STRU_FINAL. When a legacy STRU/ directory exists in the output directory, MD falls back to numbered STRU{istep} files inside that directory even if out_app_flag = 1.
[NOTE] For backward compatibility, true/false (case insensitive) are accepted and converted to 1/0.

out_hsk.description:
Output the upper triangular part of the Hamiltonian and overlap matrices in reciprocal space for each k-point into files in the directory OUT.${suffix}. The first integer selects the format:
* 0: disabled;
* 1: text output; the optional second integer controls precision and defaults to 8;
* 2: binary output in the native ABACUS .dat format;
* 3: NPZ output, which is not implemented for H(k)/S(k).

The output is also controlled by out_freq_ion and out_app_flag. For more information, refer to hs_matrix.md.
* Gamma-only, nspin = 1: hk_nao.txt for the Hamiltonian matrix and sk_nao.txt for the overlap matrix.
* Gamma-only, nspin = 2: hks1_nao.txt and hks2_nao.txt for the two spin channels of the Hamiltonian matrix, and sk_nao.txt for the overlap matrix. Only one overlap matrix is written because it is identical for both spin channels.
* Gamma-only, nspin = 4: not available with the gamma-only algorithm.
* Multi-k, nspin = 1: hk1_nao.txt for the Hamiltonian matrix and sk1_nao.txt for the overlap matrix at the first k-point.
* Multi-k, nspin = 2: hk1s1_nao.txt and hk1s2_nao.txt for the two spin channels of the Hamiltonian matrix, and sk1_nao.txt for the overlap matrix at the first k-point. Only one overlap matrix is written because it is identical for both spin channels.
* Multi-k, nspin = 4: hk1s4_nao.txt for the spinor Hamiltonian matrix and sk1_nao.txt for the spinor overlap matrix at the first k-point.
For binary output, the same names use the .dat suffix. Each native binary record contains the matrix dimension as an int followed by the row-major upper triangle. Gamma-only elements are doubles; multi-k and spinor elements are pairs of doubles containing the real and imaginary parts. Native integer representation and byte order are used.
When out_app_flag is 0, the fixed file is truncated and overwritten at every write.
When out_app_flag is 1, the first ionic step truncates the file and later steps append complete records.
When out_app_flag is 2, g followed by the one-based ionic-step index is inserted before _nao, for example hk1s1g1_nao.txt.

[NOTE] In the 3.10-LTS version, the file names are data-0-H and data-0-S, etc.

out_mat_hs.description: Legacy alias for out_hsk 1, which outputs Hamiltonian and overlap matrices in reciprocal space for each k-point. The optional second integer controls text precision. If both out_hsk and out_mat_hs are present, out_hsk takes precedence.

out_mat_hs2.description: Legacy alias for out_hsr 1, which outputs Hamiltonian and overlap matrices in real space indexed by the Bravais lattice vector R. The optional second integer controls text precision. If both out_hsr and out_mat_hs2 are present, out_hsr takes precedence.

out_mat_tk.description:
Whether to print the upper triangular part of the kinetic matrices for each k-point into OUT.${suffix}/tks1ki_nao.txt, where i is the index of k points. One may optionally provide a second parameter to specify the precision.

[NOTE] In the 3.10-LTS version, the file names are data-TR-sparse_SPIN0.csr, etc.

out_mat_r.description:
Whether to print the matrix representation of the position matrix into files named rxrs1_nao.csr, ryrs1_nao.csr, rzrs1_nao.csr in the directory OUT.${suffix}. The optional second parameter controls text output precision. If calculation is set to get_s, the position matrix can be obtained without scf iterations. For more information, please refer to position_matrix.md.

[NOTE] In the 3.10-LTS version, the file name is data-rR-sparse.csr.

out_mat_t.description:
Generate files containing the kinetic energy matrix. The optional second parameter controls text output precision. The format will be the same as the Hamiltonian matrix and overlap matrix as mentioned in out_hsr. The name of the files will be tr_nao.csr and so on. Also controled by out_freq_ion and out_app_flag.

[NOTE] In the 3.10-LTS version, the file name is data-TR-sparse_SPIN0.csr.

out_mat_dh.description:
Whether to print files containing the derivatives of the Hamiltonian matrix. The format will be the same as the Hamiltonian matrix and overlap matrix as mentioned in out_hsr. The name of the files will be dhrxs1_nao.csr, dhrys1_nao.csr, dhrzs1_nao.csr and so on. Also controled by out_freq_ion and out_app_flag.

Format: <enable> [precision] [iat1 iat2 ...]. The first value (0/1) enables/disables output. The second optional value sets the output precision (default: 8). Starting from the third value, 1-based atom indices can be listed to restrict output to derivatives with respect to those specific atoms only; if no atom indices are given, all atoms are written.

[NOTE] In the 3.10-LTS version, the file name is data-dHRx-sparse_SPIN0.csr and so on.

out_mat_dh_t.description:
Whether to print files containing the derivatives of the kinetic energy matrix dT/dR.

See out_mat_dh for format details (enable, precision, atom indices).

out_mat_dh_vl.description:
Whether to print files containing the derivatives of the local pseudopotential matrix dV^L/dR.

See out_mat_dh for format details.

out_mat_dh_vnl.description:
Whether to print files containing the derivatives of the nonlocal pseudopotential matrix dV^NL/dR.

See out_mat_dh for format details.

out_mat_dh_vh.description:
Whether to print files containing the derivatives of the Hartree matrix dV^H/dR.

See out_mat_dh for format details.

out_mat_dh_vxc.description:
Whether to print files containing the derivatives of the XC matrix dV^XC/dR.

See out_mat_dh for format details.

out_mat_h_t.description: Legacy alias for out_mat_tk, which outputs the kinetic energy matrix T(k) for each k-point in the NAO basis. The optional second integer controls text precision. If both out_mat_tk and out_mat_h_t are present, out_mat_tk takes precedence.

out_mat_vnlk.description:
Whether to print the nonlocal pseudopotential matrix Vnl(k) for each k-point in the NAO basis, into text files OUT.${suffix}/vnlk*_nao.txt.

The optional second integer controls text precision (default 8).

out_mat_h_vnl.description: Legacy alias for out_mat_vnlk, which outputs the nonlocal pseudopotential matrix Vnl(k) for each k-point in the NAO basis. The optional second integer controls text precision. If both out_mat_vnlk and out_mat_h_vnl are present, out_mat_vnlk takes precedence.

out_mat_vlk.description:
Whether to print the local pseudopotential matrix Vl(k) for each k-point in the NAO basis, into text files OUT.${suffix}/vlk*_nao.txt.

The optional second integer controls text precision (default 8).

out_mat_h_vl.description: Legacy alias for out_mat_vlk, which outputs the local pseudopotential matrix Vl(k) for each k-point in the NAO basis. The optional second integer controls text precision. If both out_mat_vlk and out_mat_h_vl are present, out_mat_vlk takes precedence.

out_mat_vhk.description:
Whether to print the Hartree matrix Vh(k) for each k-point in the NAO basis, into text files OUT.${suffix}/vhk*_nao.txt.

The optional second integer controls text precision (default 8).

out_mat_h_vh.description: Legacy alias for out_mat_vhk, which outputs the Hartree matrix Vh(k) for each k-point in the NAO basis. The optional second integer controls text precision. If both out_mat_vhk and out_mat_h_vh are present, out_mat_vhk takes precedence.

out_mat_vxck.description:
Whether to print the exchange-correlation matrix Vxc(k) for each k-point in the NAO basis, into text files OUT.${suffix}/vxck*_nao.txt.

The optional second integer controls text precision (default 8).

out_mat_h_vxc.description: Legacy alias for out_mat_vxck, which outputs the exchange-correlation matrix Vxc(k) for each k-point in the NAO basis. The optional second integer controls text precision. If both out_mat_vxck and out_mat_h_vxc are present, out_mat_vxck takes precedence.

out_mat_exxk.description:
Whether to print the exact-exchange matrix Vexx(k) for each k-point in the NAO basis, into text files OUT.${suffix}/vexxk*_nao.txt.

The optional second integer controls text precision (default 8). Only available for gamma-only calculations with exact exchange enabled.

out_mat_h_exx.description: Legacy alias for out_mat_exxk, which outputs the exact-exchange matrix Vexx(k) for each k-point in the NAO basis. The optional second integer controls text precision. If both out_mat_exxk and out_mat_h_exx are present, out_mat_exxk takes precedence.

out_mat_ds.description:
Whether to print files containing the derivatives of the overlap matrix. The optional second parameter controls text output precision. The format will be the same as the overlap matrix as mentioned in out_mat_dh. The name of the files will be dsxrs1_nao.csr and so on. Also controled by out_freq_ion and out_app_flag. This feature can be used with calculation get_s.

[NOTE] In the 3.10-LTS version, the file name is data-dSRx-sparse_SPIN0.csr and so on.

out_mat_xc.description:
Write exchange-correlation matrices in the Kohn-Sham orbital basis and their diagonal expectation values. The diagonal energies are saved in OUT.${suffix}/eband_vxc.txt. When EXX is calculated, its local and EXX contributions are also saved as eband_vxc_local.txt and eband_vxc_exx.txt in the same directory. Each energy file begins with nk, nspin, and nbands, followed by nk*nspin*nbands rows of energies in Hartree and eV.

[NOTE] In the 3.10-LTS version, the file name is k-$k-Vxc and so on.

out_mat_xc2.description:
Whether to print the exchange-correlation matrices in numerical orbital representation: in CSR format in the directory OUT.${suffix}. The name of the files will be vxcrs1_nao.csr and so on.

[NOTE] In the 3.10-LTS version, the file name is Vxc_R_spin$s and so on.

out_mat_l.description: Whether to print the expectation value of the angular momentum operator , , and in the basis of the localized atomic orbitals.
