The files are named lx_nao.txt, ly_nao.txt, and lz_nao.txt (or lxg{step+1}_nao.txt etc. when out_app_flag = 2). The second integer controls the precision of the output.

out_xc_r.description:
The first integer controls whether to output the exchange-correlation (in Bohr^-3) on real space grids using Libxc to folder OUT.${suffix}:
* 0: rho, amag, sigma, exc
* 1: vrho, vsigma
* 2: v2rho2, v2rhosigma, v2sigma2
* 3: v3rho3, v3rho2sigma, v3rhosigma2, v3sigma3
* 4: v4rho4, v4rho3sigma, v4rho2sigma2, v4rhosigma3, v4sigma4 The meaning of the files is presented in Libxc

The second integer controls the precision of the charge density output, if not given, will use 3 as default.

The circle order of the charge density on real space grids is: x is the outer loop, then y and finally z (z is moving fastest).

out_eband.description: Whether to print the band-decomposed energy of each Hamiltonian term in the files eband_kin.txt, eband_vl.txt, eband_vnl.txt, eband_hart.txt and eband_vxc.txt under the output directory. Each file starts with comment lines giving the ABACUS version, the timestamp, the ionic step and total energy, the expectation-value formula, and the units. The terms include the kinetic, pseudopotential (local + nonlocal), Hartree and exchange-correlation (including exact exchange if calculated).

out_eband_terms.description: Legacy alias for out_eband, which outputs the band-decomposed energy of each Hamiltonian term. If both out_eband and out_eband_terms are present, out_eband takes precedence.

out_hr_npz.description: Whether to print Hamiltonian matrices H(R) in NPZ format as hrs1_nao.npz and, for nspin = 2, hrs2_nao.npz. This feature does not work for gamma-only calculations.

out_hsr_npz.description: Legacy alias for out_hsr 3, writing hrs1_nao.npz, hrs2_nao.npz when needed, and sr_nao.npz. If both out_hsr and out_hsr_npz are present, out_hsr takes precedence. Gamma-only calculations write the folded R = (0, 0, 0) representation.

out_dm_npz.description: Whether to print density matrices DM(R) in npz format. This feature does not work for gamma-only calculations.

out_mul.description: Whether to print the Mulliken population analysis result into OUT.${suffix}/mulliken.txt. In molecular dynamics calculations, the output frequency is controlled by out_freq_ion.

out_app_flag.description:
Controls output file organization during multi-step calculations (MD, relax, RT-TDDFT). The directory routing applies to both LCAO and PW basis calculations.
* 0: Write directly to the OUT directory under a fixed filename. Every write truncates the previous content, so only the most recently written step is kept on disk. out_freq_ion only controls how often a write happens; it does not change the number of fixed-name files (default, disk-friendly). Exception: MD structure frames are still written as numbered STRU{istep} files, so their count follows out_freq_ion.
* 1: Reuse fixed filenames across steps: text outputs append new records, cube outputs accumulate one frame per written step
  In mode 1 the first output step of a fresh (non-restart) run truncates the fixed-name file so a rerun does not keep stale records from a previous run; later steps and restarted runs keep appending.
* 2: Write to subdirectory (STRUC/ for structure files, PSI/, CHG/, POT/, ELF/, DOS/, DIP/, MAT/), output data files carry a g{step} suffix (structures use STRU{istep})
For MD structure frames specifically, mode 0 keeps the numbered STRU{istep} files (STRU1 is the initial geometry) and writes no STRU_NOW, mode 1 writes one cumulative STRU file, and mode 2 writes the numbered files under STRUC/; see out_stru.
The legacy Boolean spellings (true/false, yes/no, on/off, t/f, y/n, and the dotted forms) are still accepted: true maps to mode 1 and preserves the old append behavior; false maps to mode 0, which now overwrites a fixed file instead of the old g{step} per-step files, so use mode 2 to reproduce that old behavior.
For more information, refer to the documentation of out_mat_r, out_hsr, out_mat_t, out_mat_dh, out_hsk, out_wfc_lcao, out_chg, out_pot, out_elf, out_dos, out_dipole, out_stru.

out_ndigits.description: Controls the length of decimal part of output data, such as charge density, Hamiltonian matrix, Overlap matrix and so on.

out_element_info.description: Whether to print element information into files in the directory OUT.{element_label}, including pseudopotential and orbital information of the element (in atomic Ryberg units).

restart_save.description:
Whether to save charge density files per ionic step, which are used to restart calculations. According to the value of read_file_dir:
* auto: These files are saved in folder OUT.{read_file_dir}/restart/.

If EXX(exact exchange) is calculated (i.e. dft_fuctional==hse/hf/pbe0/scan0 or rpa==True), the Hexx(R) files for each processor will also be saved in the above folder, which can be read in EXX calculation with restart_load==True.

rpa.description:
Generate output files used in rpa calculations.

[NOTE] If symmetry is set to 1, additional files containing the necessary information for exploiting symmetry in the subsequent rpa calculation will be output: irreducible_sector.txt, symrot_k.txt and symrot_R.txt.

rpa_out_vel.description: Velocity matrix in KS basis (in unit of eV *Angstrom). Loop layer: spin -> k -> direction -> KS_basis1 -> KS_basis2.

rpa_outdir.description: The directory to save files for LibRPA.

out_librpa_ver.description: Select the LibRPA file protocol: 0 for legacy text output and 1 for reader-v1 output. Reader-v1 supports symmetry-reduced Monkhorst-Pack grids and requires a uniform Monkhorst-Pack KPT grid.

out_pchg.description:
Selects electronic states for partial (band-decomposed) charge-density output using a space-separated string of `0`s and `1`s, where `1` selects a state and `0` skips it. Repetition follows the `ocp_set` syntax, for example `1 4*0 5*1 0`; the expanded list must not exceed `nbands`. Each output represents a complete one-particle state. The spin degeneracy is 2 for `nspin=1` and 1 for `nspin=2` or `nspin=4`. For `nspin=1`, `s1` contains the charge density. For `nspin=2`, `s1` and `s2` contain the spin-up and spin-down charge densities, respectively. For `nspin=4`, `s1`, `s2`, `s3`, and `s4` respectively contain $\rho_0$, $m_x$, $m_y$, and $m_z$. With `if_separate_k=true`, files are named `pchgi[state]s[component]k[kpoint].cube`; otherwise, the weighted k-point sum is named `pchgi[state]s[component].cube`.

For PW calculations with ultrasoft pseudopotentials (USPP), the single-state valence density includes the augmentation contribution:

$$
\rho_{n\boldsymbol{k}}(\boldsymbol{r})=\left\vert\tilde{\psi}_{n\boldsymbol{k}}(\boldsymbol{r})\right\vert^2+\sum_{Iij}Q_{ij}^{I}(\boldsymbol{r})\Braket{\tilde{\psi}_{n\boldsymbol{k}} | \beta_i^I}\Braket{\beta_j^I | \tilde{\psi}_{n\boldsymbol{k}}}.
$$

Here $\tilde{\psi}$ is the pseudo-wavefunction, $\beta_i^I$ are the atomic projectors, and $Q_{ij}^I$ are the augmentation functions. Each separate-k output has a cell integral equal to the spin degeneracy. The merged output uses k-point weights including spin degeneracy, and its integral equals their sum for the corresponding spin channel.

[NOTE] Enabling symmetry may produce unintended partial charge densities because of reduced k-point weights and real-space symmetry operations. If the desired symmetry treatment is uncertain, set `symmetry = -1`. Use the same symmetry setting as in the SCF calculation.

out_wfc_norm.description: Selects electronic states for real-space wavefunction-modulus output using the selection syntax of `out_pchg`. Each output contains single-particle wavefunction amplitudes. In PW calculations, norm-conserving pseudo-wavefunctions satisfy $\Braket{\psi_{n\boldsymbol{k}} | \psi_{n\boldsymbol{k}}}=1$, while USPP pseudo-wavefunctions satisfy $\Braket{\tilde{\psi}_{n\boldsymbol{k}} | \hat{S} | \tilde{\psi}_{n\boldsymbol{k}}}=1$, where $\hat{S}=1+\sum_{Iij}q_{ij}^I\Ket{\beta_i^I}\Bra{\beta_j^I}$ is the USPP overlap operator, $q_{ij}^I=\int Q_{ij}^I(\boldsymbol{r})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{r}$, and $\beta_i^I$ are the atomic projectors. For `nspin=1`, `s1` contains the wavefunction modulus. For `nspin=2`, `s1` and `s2` contain the spin-up and spin-down wavefunction moduli, respectively. For `nspin=4`, `s1` contains the total spinor modulus. Files are named `wfi[state]s[spin]k[kpoint].cube`.

out_wfc_re_im.description: Selects electronic states for real-space wavefunction real- and imaginary-part output using the selection syntax of `out_pchg`. Each output contains single-particle wavefunction amplitudes. In PW calculations, norm-conserving pseudo-wavefunctions satisfy $\Braket{\psi_{n\boldsymbol{k}} | \psi_{n\boldsymbol{k}}}=1$, while USPP pseudo-wavefunctions satisfy $\Braket{\tilde{\psi}_{n\boldsymbol{k}} | \hat{S} | \tilde{\psi}_{n\boldsymbol{k}}}=1$, where $\hat{S}=1+\sum_{Iij}q_{ij}^I\Ket{\beta_i^I}\Bra{\beta_j^I}$ is the USPP overlap operator, $q_{ij}^I=\int Q_{ij}^I(\boldsymbol{r})\,\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{r}$, and $\beta_i^I$ are the atomic projectors. For `nspin=1`, `s1` contains the wavefunction. For `nspin=2`, `s1` and `s2` contain the spin-up and spin-down wavefunctions, respectively. For `nspin=4`, `s1` and `s2` contain the upper and lower spinor components, respectively. Files are named `wfi[state]s[spin]k[kpoint][re/im].cube`.

if_separate_k.description: Specifies whether to write partial charge densities for individual k-points or merge them.
if_separate_k.availability: (basis_type==pw and out_pchg!=none) or (basis_type==lcao and calculation==get_pchg and gamma_only==0)

out_elf.description:
Whether to output the electron localization function (ELF) in the folder `OUT.${suffix}`. The files are named as
* nspin = 1:
    * elftot.cube: ${\rm{ELF}} = \frac{1}{1+\chi^2}$, $\chi = \frac{\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i}{f_i |\nabla\psi_{i}|^2} - \frac{|\nabla\rho|^2}{8\rho}}{\frac{3}{10}(3\pi^2)^{2/3}\rho^{5/3}}$;
* nspin = 2:
    * elfs1.cube, elfs2.cube: ${\rm{ELF}}_\sigma = \frac{1}{1+\chi_\sigma^2}$, $\chi_\sigma = \frac{\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i}{f_i |\nabla\psi_{i,\sigma}|^2} - \frac{|\nabla\rho_\sigma|^2}{8\rho_\sigma}}{\frac{3}{10}(6\pi^2)^{2/3}\rho_\sigma^{5/3}}$;
    * elftot.cube: ${\rm{ELF}} = \frac{1}{1+\chi^2}$, $\chi = \frac{\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i,\sigma}{f_i |\nabla\psi_{i,\sigma}|^2} - \sum_{\sigma}{\frac{|\nabla\rho_\sigma|^2}{8\rho_\sigma}}}{\sum_{\sigma}{\frac{3}{10}(6\pi^2)^{2/3}\rho_\sigma^{5/3}}}$;
* nspin = 4 (noncollinear):
    * elftot.cube: ELF for total charge density, ${\rm{ELF}} = \frac{1}{1+\chi^2}$, $\chi = \frac{\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i}{f_i |\nabla\psi_{i}|^2} - \frac{|\nabla\rho|^2}{8\rho}}{\frac{3}{10}(3\pi^2)^{2/3}\rho^{5/3}}$

With `out_app_flag=0` the fixed-name files (`elftot.cube`, `elfs1.cube`) are truncated and overwritten at every write.
With `out_app_flag=1` the geometry step suffix is omitted and the same ELF files accumulate one complete cube frame per written ionic step (`Ionic_Step {#}` as the first comment line, one-based); the first written step truncates them.
With `out_app_flag=2`, every written step gets its own suffixed file (e.g., `elftotg1.cube`, `elfs1g1.cube`) routed to the `ELF/` subdirectory.

The second integer controls the precision of the kinetic energy density output, if not given, will use 3 as default. For purpose restarting from this file and other high-precision involved calculation, recommend to use 10.

In molecular dynamics calculations, the output frequency is controlled by out_freq_ion.

out_spillage.description: This output is only intentively needed by the ABACUS numerical atomic orbital generation workflow. This parameter is used to control whether to output the overlap integrals between truncated spherical Bessel functions (TSBFs) and plane-wave basis expanded wavefunctions (named as OVERLAP_Q), and between TSBFs (named as OVERLAP_Sq), also their first order derivatives. The output files are named starting with orb_matrix. A value of 2 would enable the output.

out_dipole.description:
Output the electronic dipole moment to `OUT.{suffix}/dipole_s[spin].txt`. In Hartree atomic units,

$$\boldsymbol{P}(t)=-\int_{\Omega}\boldsymbol{r}\,\rho(\boldsymbol{r},t)\,\mathrm{d}^3r,$$

where the integral is over the simulation cell and $\rho$ is the electron number density. For `nspin=2`, the two spin channels are written separately; for `nspin=1` or `4`, a single file contains the dipole of the total electron density.

Each row contains the step index followed by $P_x$, $P_y$, and $P_z$. The running log additionally reports the ionic and combined dipoles.

* `True`: Enable dipole output.
* `False`: Disable dipole output.

out_current.description:
Output the RT-TDDFT charge current density. In Hartree atomic units,

$$\boldsymbol{J}(t)=-\frac{1}{\Omega}\sum_{n\boldsymbol{k}}f_{n\boldsymbol{k}}\operatorname{Re}\Braket{\psi_{n\boldsymbol{k}}(t)|\hat{\boldsymbol{v}}(t)|\psi_{n\boldsymbol{k}}(t)},$$

where $\Omega$ is the cell volume, $f_{n\boldsymbol{k}}$ includes occupations and k-point weights, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{v}}$ is the velocity operator.

* `0`: Disable current output.
* `1`: Available for PW and LCAO. Evaluate the velocity from momentum and nonlocal pseudopotential contributions, including coupling to the vector potential in the velocity gauge. Other nonlocal terms, such as exact exchange, are not included. Write the total current to `OUT.{suffix}/current_tot.txt`.
* `2`: Available only for LCAO. Construct the velocity matrix from the full Hamiltonian in the nonorthogonal atomic-orbital basis: $\widetilde{v}_{\alpha}=\partial_{k_{\alpha}}H+\mathrm{i}HS^{-1}\mathcal{R}_{\alpha}-\mathrm{i}\mathcal{R}_{\alpha}S^{-1}H-HS^{-1}\partial_{k_{\alpha}}S$, where $H$, $S$, and $\mathcal{R}_{\alpha}$ are the Hamiltonian, overlap, and position matrices in k space. This automatically includes nonlocal contributions present in the Hamiltonian, including exact exchange. Write the total current to `OUT.{suffix}/current_tot_comm.txt`.

Each row contains the step index followed by $J_x$, $J_y$, and $J_z$.

out_current_k.description:
Controls whether RT-TDDFT current density is also resolved by spin and k-point. PW supports `out_current=1`; LCAO supports `out_current=1` or `2`. The total-current file is always written when current output is enabled.
* `True`: In addition to the total, `out_current=1` writes `OUT.{suffix}/current_s[spin]k[kpoint].txt`; `out_current=2` writes `OUT.{suffix}/current_s[spin]k[kpoint]_comm.txt`. These weighted contributions sum to the total current.
* `False`: Output only `current_tot.txt` for `out_current=1` or `current_tot_comm.txt` for `out_current=2`.
out_current_k.availability: basis_type in [pw, lcao] and esolver_type==tddft and out_current>0

out_efield.description:
Controls time-dependent electric-field output in `OUT.{suffix}/`. `efield_total.txt` contains time in fs followed by the total-field components $E_x$, $E_y$, and $E_z$ in V/Angstrom. Each configured analytic field is additionally written to `efield_[index].txt`, containing time in fs and the field value in V/Angstrom. The index follows the occurrence order in `td_ttype` and `td_vext_dire`; fields assigned to the same direction remain in separate files. Output is written on active electronic steps. Fresh calculations overwrite the output; runs with `md_restart=True` append to it.
* `True`: Output electric-field values.
* `False`: Do not output electric-field values.

out_vecpot.description:
Controls vector-potential output to `OUT.{suffix}/vector_pot.txt`. Each row contains the step index followed by $A_x$, $A_y$, and $A_z$ in Hartree atomic units. The file can be used as input for `init_vecpot` with the same `td_dt`. Fresh calculations overwrite the output; runs with `md_restart=True` append to it.
* `True`: Output the vector potential.
* `False`: Do not output the vector potential.
out_vecpot.availability: esolver_type==tddft and ((basis_type==pw and td_stype==1) or (basis_type==lcao and td_stype in [1, 2]))

cal_symm_repr.description: Whether to print the matrix representation of symmetry operation to running log file. If the first value is given as 1, then all matrix representations will be printed. The second optional parameter controls the precision (number of digits) to print, default is 3, which is enough for a quick check.

spillage_outdir.description: The directory to save the spillage files.

dos_edelta_ev.description: The step size in writing Density of States (DOS). The default value was changed from 0.01 to 0.03 eV.

dos_sigma.description: The width of the Gaussian factor when obtaining smeared Density of States (DOS)

dos_scale.description: Defines the energy range of DOS output as (emax-emin)*(1+dos_scale), centered at (emax+emin)/2. This parameter will be used when dos_emin and dos_emax are not set.

dos_emin_ev.description:
The minimal range for Density of States (DOS)
* If set, "dos_scale" will be ignored.

dos_emax_ev.description:
The maximal range for Density of States (DOS)
* If set, "dos_scale" will be ignored.

dos_nche.description: The order of Chebyshev expansions when using Stochastic Density Functional Theory (SDFT) to calculate DOS.

stm_bias.description:
The bias voltage used to calculate local density of states to simulate scanning tunneling microscope, see details in out_ldos. When using three parameters:

* The first parameter specifies the initial bias voltage value.
* The second parameter defines the voltage increment (step size between consecutive bias values).
* The third parameter determines the total number of voltage points

ldos_line.description: Specify the path of the three-dimensional space and display LDOS in the form of a two-dimensional color chart, see details in out_ldos. The first three paramenters are the direct coordinates of the start point, the next three paramenters are the direct coordinates of the end point, and the final one is the number of points along the path, whose default is 100.

cond_che_thr.description: Control the error of Chebyshev expansions for conductivities.

cond_dt.description: Time interval () to integrate Onsager coefficients.

cond_dtbatch.description:
exp(iH\dt\cond_dtbatch) is expanded with Chebyshev expansion to calculate conductivities. It is faster but costs more memory.
* If cond_dtbatch = 0: Autoset this parameter to make expansion orders larger than 100.

cond_smear.description:
Smearing method for conductivities
* 1: Gaussian smearing
* 2: Lorentzian smearing

cond_fwhm.description: FWHM for conductivities. For Gaussian smearing, ; for Lorentzian smearing, .

cond_nonlocal.description:
Whether to consider nonlocal potential correction when calculating velocity matrix .
* True: .
* False: .

berry_phase.description:
Controls the calculation of Berry phase
* true: Calculate Berry phase.
* false: Do not calculate Berry phase.

gdir.description:
The direction of the polarization in the lattice vector for Berry phase calculation
* 1: Calculate the polarization in the direction of the lattice vector a_1 defined in the STRU file.
* 2: Calculate the polarization in the direction of the lattice vector a_2 defined in the STRU file.
* 3: Calculate the polarization in the direction of the lattice vector a_3 defined in the STRU file.

towannier90.description:
Controls the generation of files for the Wannier90 code.
* 1: Generate files for the Wannier90 code.
* 0: Do not generate files for the Wannier90 code.

nnkpfile.description: The file name generated when running "wannier90 -pp ..." command

wannier_method.description:
Only available on LCAO basis, using different methods to generate "\.mmn" file and "\.amn" file.
* 1: Calculated using the lcao_in_pw method, the calculation accuracy can be improved by increasing ecutwfc to maintain consistency with the pw basis set results.
* 2: The overlap between atomic orbitals is calculated using grid integration. The radial grid points are generated using the Gauss-Legendre method, while the spherical grid points are generated using the Lebedev-Laikov method.

wannier_spin.description:
The spin direction for the Wannier function calculation when nspin is set to 2
* up: Calculate spin up for the Wannier function.
* down: Calculate spin down for the Wannier function.

out_wannier_mmn.description:
Write the "*.mmn" file or not.
* 0: don't write the "*.mmn" file.
* 1: write the "*.mmn" file.

out_wannier_amn.description:
Write the "*.amn" file or not.
* 0: don't write the "*.amn" file.
* 1: write the "*.amn" file.

out_wannier_eig.description:
Write the "*.eig" file or not.
* 0: don't write the "*.eig" file.
* 1: write the "*.eig" file.

out_wannier_spn.description: Write <seedname>.spn with the x, y, z Pauli matrix elements. Set spinors=true and spn_formatted=true in the Wannier90 input.
out_wannier_spn.default: 1 when the output requirements are met, 0 otherwise
out_wannier_spn.requirements: When out_wannier_spn==true: require towannier90==true and calculation==nscf and basis_type==lcao and wannier_method==2 and nspin==4

out_wannier_unk.description:
Write the "UNK.*" file or not.
* 0: don't write the "UNK.*" file.
* 1: write the "UNK.*" file.

out_wannier_wvfn_formatted.description:
Write the "UNK.*" file in ASCII format or binary format.
* 0: write the "UNK.*" file in binary format.
* 1: write the "UNK.*" file in ASCII format (text file format).

efield_flag.description:
Added the electric field.
* True: A saw-like potential simulating an electric field is added to the bare ionic potential.
* False: Not added the electric field.
[NOTE] LR-TDDFT excited-state forces and relaxation do not support this external field: the moving-AO correction is not implemented.

dip_cor_flag.description:
Added a dipole correction to the bare ionic potential.
* True: A dipole correction is also added to the bare ionic potential.
* False: A dipole correction is not added to the bare ionic potential.

[NOTE] Note: If you do not want any electric field, the parameter efield_amp should be set to zero. This should ONLY be used in a slab geometry for surface calculations, with the discontinuity FALLING IN THE EMPTY SPACE.

efield_dir.description:
The direction of the electric field or dipole correction is parallel to the reciprocal lattice vector, so the potential is constant in planes defined by FFT grid points, efield_dir can set to 0, 1 or 2.
* 0: parallel to the first reciprocal lattice vector
* 1: parallel to the second reciprocal lattice vector
* 2: parallel to the third reciprocal lattice vector
efield_dir.requirements: When gate_flag==true and efield_flag==true: require dip_cor_flag==true

efield_pos_max.description: Position of the maximum of the saw-like potential along crystal axis efield_dir, within the unit cell, 0 <= efield_pos_max < 1.
efield_pos_max.default: Autoset to center of vacuum - width of vacuum / 20

efield_pos_dec.description: Zone in the unit cell where the saw-like potential decreases, 0 < efield_pos_dec < 1.

efield_amp.description:
Amplitude of the electric field. The saw-like potential increases with slope efield_amp in the region from efield_pos_max+efield_pos_dec-1) to (efield_pos_max), then decreases until (efield_pos_max+efield_pos_dec), in units of the crystal vector efield_dir.

[NOTE] Note: The change of slope of this potential must be located in the empty region, or else unphysical forces will result.

gate_flag.description:
Controls the addition of compensating charge by a charged plate for charged cells.
* true: A charged plate is placed at the zgate position to add compensating charge. The direction is determined by efield_dir.
* false: No compensating charge is added.

zgate.description: Position of the charged plate in the unit cell

block.description:
Controls the addition of a potential barrier to prevent electron spillover.
* true: A potential barrier is added from block_down to block_up with a height of block_height. If dip_cor_flag is set to true, efield_pos_dec is used to smoothly increase and decrease the potential barrier.
* false: No potential barrier is added.

block_down.description: Lower beginning of the potential barrier

block_up.description: Upper beginning of the potential barrier

imp_sol.description:
Implicit solvation model:
* 0: no implicit solvent.
* 1: the original ABACUS implicit solvation model.
* 2: the self-consistent continuum solvation model (SCCS). Supported scope: CPU KS-DFT (esolver_type ksdft, device cpu) with basis_type pw or lcao; calculation scf (energies and forces) or fixed-cell relax, no stress (cal_stress and cell-relax are rejected); nspin 1 or 2; assume_isolated none, pcc_0d or pcc_2d; no electric/gate field, DFT-1/2, DeePKS or dm_to_rho. Use assume_isolated pcc_0d or pcc_2d for charged systems: with assume_isolated none a charged cell only prints a warning and runs, and its energy then depends on the cell size because the periodic Poisson solver drops the G = 0 net charge. With pcc_0d or pcc_2d, see sccs_lowpass_p1 for the accuracy of forces.

Legacy Boolean values (true/false) are read as 1/0.

eb_k.description: The relative permittivity of the bulk solvent, 80 for water

tau.description: The effective surface tension parameter that describes the cavitation, the dispersion, and the repulsion interaction between the solute and the solvent which are not captured by the electrostatic terms

sigma_k.description: The width of the diffuse cavity that is implicitly determined by the electronic structure of the solute

nc_k.description: The value of the electron density at which the dielectric cavity forms

sccs_preset.description: SCCS parameter preset. Allowed values: custom, vacuum, water-neutral, water-cation, water-anion. Non-custom presets override sccs_epsilon, sccs_rho_min, sccs_rho_max, sccs_gamma and sccs_pressure; solver controls and surface regularization remain user-controlled.

sccs_epsilon.description: Bulk dielectric constant >= 1 for the custom preset. The default 1 (no dielectric) follows the Environ env_static_permittivity default for environ_type input. Water presets use 78.3 and vacuum uses 1.

sccs_rho_min.description: Lower electronic-density cavity threshold for the custom preset. Water-neutral/vacuum: 1e-4; water-cation: 2e-4; water-anion: 2.4e-3.

sccs_rho_max.description: Upper electronic-density cavity threshold for the custom preset. Water-neutral/vacuum: 5e-3; water-cation: 3.5e-3; water-anion: 1.55e-2.

sccs_gamma.description: Surface coefficient for the custom preset. Water-neutral: 47.9; water-cation: 5; water-anion/vacuum: 0.

sccs_pressure.description: Volume coefficient for the custom preset. Water-neutral: -0.36; water-cation: 0.125; water-anion: 0.45; vacuum: 0.

sccs_maxiter.description: Positive maximum number of SCCS sqrt-CG iterations. Failure to satisfy both residual tolerances terminates the calculation.

sccs_tol_rms.description: Positive RMS charge-residual tolerance for the SCCS sqrt-CG solver.

sccs_tol_max.description: Positive maximum charge-residual tolerance for the SCCS sqrt-CG solver.

sccs_surface_eta.description: Positive regularization of the SCCS surface gradient norm.

sccs_lowpass_p1.description: Low-pass filter of the SCCS switching-function derivatives, as Environ deriv_lowpass_p1 with deriv_method fft. Only with assume_isolated pcc_0d or pcc_2d. The default -1 turns it off, which reproduces Environ deriv_method fft (continuum cavity potential) for the plain cavity; the solvent-aware cavity then differentiates the filling analytically on the FFT derivatives of the local cavity. With lowpass disabled (the default), analytical forces may differ from finite differences of the self-consistent energy. For geometry optimization with PCC, consider enabling lowpass and check force accuracy against finite differences. With lowpass disabled, the cavity potential uses the FFT gradient of the PCC-corrected potential, which oscillates around the potential step at the cell boundary half a cell from the system center; keep the dielectric transition region several bohr away from that boundary. Typical values are sccs_lowpass_p1 10 and sccs_lowpass_p2 5. The filter changes the model energy, so compare only results computed with the same values.

sccs_lowpass_p2.description: Offset of the SCCS switching-function low-pass filter, as Environ deriv_lowpass_p2; see sccs_lowpass_p1. Both must be positive or both non-positive. Default -1 (off).

sccs_solvent_mode.description: Allowed values: electronic (default) and full, as Environ solvent_mode. electronic builds the dielectric cavity from the valence electron density. full adds valence-charge Gaussians selected by sccs_corespread.

sccs_corespread.description: Widths of the valence-charge Gaussians used only with sccs_solvent_mode full. One value applies to every atom except those whose known atomic number equals the pseudopotential valence charge (within 1e-8). More than one value requires exactly nat values in STRU atom order (grouped by atom type), and overrides this automatic exclusion. A value <= 0 disables the cavity Gaussian on that atom. A per-atom list sets symmetry 1 to 0, because the symmetry analysis does not distinguish equivalent atoms by their widths.

sccs_solvent_radius.description: Solvent radius in bohr of the solvent-aware SCCS cavity, as Environ solvent_radius (Andreussi et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput. 15, 1996 (2019)). A positive value fills the parts of the cavity that a probe sphere of radius sccs_radial_scale * sccs_solvent_radius cannot reach, for example small voids between atoms. Unlike Environ, the probe sums all periodic images within its cutoff, so cells narrower than the probe are not truncated. With PCC, see also sccs_lowpass_p1. Non-negative; default 0 (off).

sccs_radial_scale.description: Probe radius of the solvent-aware SCCS cavity in units of sccs_solvent_radius, as Environ radial_scale; at least 1, default 2. Used only when sccs_solvent_radius is positive.

sccs_radial_spread.description: erfc spread of the solvent-aware probe sphere, as Environ radial_spread; positive, default 0.5 bohr. Used only when sccs_solvent_radius is positive.

sccs_filling_thr.description: Solute fraction of the solvent-aware probe sphere above which a point is filled, as Environ filling_threshold; between 0 and 1 (exclusive), default 0.825. Used only when sccs_solvent_radius is positive.

sccs_filling_spread.description: Width of the erfc step of the solvent-aware filling in the probe solute fraction, as Environ filling_spread; positive, default 0.02. Used only when sccs_solvent_radius is positive. As in Environ, open solvent is filled by erfc(sccs_filling_thr / sccs_filling_spread) / 2, which lowers the bulk permittivity: below 1e-17 up to a spread of sccs_filling_thr / 6, but 1e-2 at 0.5.

sccs_start_drho.description: Delays the start of SCCS until DRHO is at or below this value; until then the SCF runs without the solvent, while PCC, if set, stays on. 0 (default) starts SCCS immediately. A positive value must be larger than scf_thr, so that the SCF cannot converge before SCCS starts. When SCCS starts, the charge mixing restarts, that iteration does not count as converged, and the iteration is printed on the screen. SCCS then stays on for the rest of the run, including later ionic steps. Not set by sccs_preset.

sccs_start_nmax.description: With sccs_start_drho > 0, starts SCCS at this electronic iteration at the latest, if DRHO has not yet reached sccs_start_drho. Must be positive, and smaller than scf_nmax when sccs_start_drho > 0. Default 30. Not set by sccs_preset.

sccs_debug.description: Level of the SCCS reports, written to the running log (running_*.log in OUT.{suffix}): 0 (default) writes none; 1 writes the sqrt-CG iteration count and the correction energies of every SCF iteration; 2 also writes the residuals, warm start, cavity volume and surface (with the solvent-aware filled volume), the FFT counts of the Coulomb operator in the sqrt-CG solve and the count of reused fixed sources, and with PCC the Gauss-law check (far-field polarization charge and its expected value), the charge moments and the energy components.

vdw_method.description:
Specifies the method used for Van der Waals (VdW) correction. Available options are:
* d2: Grimme's D2 dispersion correction method
* d3_0: Grimme's DFT-D3(0) dispersion correction method (zero-damping)
* d3_bj: Grimme's DFTD3(BJ) dispersion correction method (BJ-damping)
* d4: Grimme's DFT-D4 dispersion correction method using the external DFT-D4 library
* none: no vdW correction

[NOTE] ABACUS automatically loads DFT-D3 parameters for supported functionals according to dft_functional setting. Individual user values overwrite the corresponding tabulated values. Setting all four of vdw_s6, vdw_s8, vdw_a1 and vdw_a2 defines a fully custom set and bypasses functional lookup.

vdw_d4_xc.description:
Functional name used to load DFT-D4 damping parameters from the DFT-D4 library.
If set to default, ABACUS infers the functional name from dft_functional or pseudopotential metadata.

vdw_d4_model.description:
DFT-D4 dispersion model used by the external DFT-D4 library.
Available options are:
* d4: standard D4 model
* d4s: smooth D4S model

vdw_s6.description: Scale factor s6, which is used to optimize the interaction energy deviations in van der Waals (vdW) corrected calculations. The recommended values of this parameter are dependent on the chosen vdW correction method and the DFT functional being used. For DFT-D2, the recommended values are 0.75 (PBE), 1.2 (BLYP), 1.05 (B-P86), 1.0 (TPSS), and 1.05 (B3LYP); if not set, will use values of PBE functional by default. For DFT-D3, ABACUS will search in built-in dataset based on the dft_functional setting by default; user set value will overwrite the searched value.

vdw_s8.description: Scale factor s8 for D3(0) and D3(BJ). By default, ABACUS will search in built-in dataset based on the dft_functional setting. User set value will overwrite the searched value.

vdw_a1.description: Damping parameter rs6 for D3(0), or a1 for D3(BJ). If not set, ABACUS loads the s-dftd3 value for dft_functional. A user value overwrites the tabulated value.

vdw_a2.description: Damping parameter rs8 for D3(0), or a2 for D3(BJ). If not set, ABACUS loads the s-dftd3 value for dft_functional. A user value overwrites the tabulated value.

vdw_d.description: Controls the damping rate of the damping function in the DFT-D2 method.

vdw_abc.description:
Determines whether three-body terms are calculated for DFT-D3 methods.
* True: ABACUS will calculate the three-body term.
* False: The three-body term is not included.

vdw_c6_file.description:
Specifies the name of the file containing parameters for each element when using the D2 method. If not set, ABACUS uses the default parameters (Jnm6/mol) stored in the program. To manually set the parameters, provide a file containing the parameters. An example is given by:

H 0.1 Si 9.0

Namely, each line contains the element name and the corresponding parameter.

vdw_c6_unit.description:
Specifies the unit of the provided parameters in the D2 method. Available options are:
* Jnm6/mol (J nm^6/mol)
* eVA (eV Angstrom)

vdw_r0_file.description:
Specifies the name of the file containing parameters for each element when using the D2 method. If not set, ABACUS uses the default parameters (Angstrom) stored in the program. To manually set the parameters, provide a file containing the parameters. An example is given by:

Li 1.0 Cl 2.0

Namely, each line contains the element name and the corresponding parameter.

vdw_r0_unit.description:
Specifies the unit for the parameters in the D2 method when manually set by the user. Available options are:
* A (Angstrom)
* Bohr

vdw_cutoff_type.description:
Determines the method used for specifying the cutoff radius in periodic systems when applying Van der Waals correction. Available options are:
* radius: The supercell is selected within a sphere centered at the origin with a radius defined by vdw_cutoff_radius.
* period: The extent of the D2 supercell is explicitly specified using the vdw_cutoff_period keyword. DFT-D3 and DFT-D4 require radius.
vdw_cutoff_type.requirements: When vdw_method in [d3_0, d3_bj, d4]: require vdw_cutoff_type==radius

vdw_cutoff_radius.description: Defines the radius of the cutoff sphere when vdw_cutoff_type is set to radius. The default values depend on the chosen vdw_method.

vdw_radius_unit.description:
Specify the unit of vdw_cutoff_radius. Available options are:
* A(Angstrom)
* Bohr

vdw_cutoff_width2.description:
Width of the smooth switching region for the two-body pairwise dispersion real-space cutoff.
A value of zero disables smoothing for the two-body contribution.

vdw_cutoff_width3.description:
Width of the smooth switching region for the three-body Axilrod-Teller-Muto (ATM) dispersion real-space cutoff.
A value of zero disables smoothing for the three-body contribution.

vdw_cutoff_period.description: The three integers supplied here explicitly specify the extent of the supercell in the directions of the three basis lattice vectors.

vdw_cn_thr.description: The cutoff radius when calculating coordination numbers.

vdw_cn_thr_unit.description:
Unit of the coordination number cutoff (vdw_cn_thr). Available options are:
* A(Angstrom)
* Bohr

exx_fock_alpha.description: Fraction of full-ranged Fock exchange $1/r$ in range-separated hybrid functionals.

exx_erfc_alpha.description: Fraction of short-ranged Fock exchange $\mathrm{erfc}(\omega r)/r$ in range-separated hybrid functionals.

exx_erfc_omega.description: Range-separation parameter $\omega$ in the short-ranged Fock term $\mathrm{erfc}(\omega r)/r$.

exx_separate_loop.description:
There are two types of iterative approaches provided by ABACUS to evaluate Fock exchange.
* False: Start with a GGA-Loop, and then Hybrid-Loop, in which EXX Hamiltonian is updated with electronic iterations.
* True: A two-step method is employed, i.e. in the inner iterations, density matrix is updated, while in the outer iterations, is calculated based on density matrix that converges in the inner iteration.

exx_hybrid_step.description: The maximal iteration number of the outer-loop, where the Fock exchange is calculated

exx_mixing_beta.description: Mixing parameter for densty matrix in each iteration of the outer-loop

exx_fock_lambda.description: It is used to compensate for divergence points at G=0 in the evaluation of Fock exchange using lcao_in_pw method.

exx_pca_threshold.description: To accelerate the evaluation of four-center integrals (), the product of atomic orbitals are expanded in the basis of auxiliary basis functions (ABF): . The size of the ABF (i.e. number of ) is reduced using principal component analysis. When a large PCA threshold is used, the number of ABF will be reduced, hence the calculation becomes faster. However, this comes at the cost of computational accuracy. A relatively safe choice of the value is 1e-4.

exx_c_threshold.description: See also the entry exx_pca_threshold. Smaller components (less than exx_c_threshold) of the matrix are neglected to accelerate calculation. The larger the threshold is, the faster the calculation and the lower the accuracy. A relatively safe choice of the value is 1e-4.

exx_cs_inv_thr.description: By default, the Coulomb matrix inversion required for obtaining LRI coefficients is performed using Cholesky factorization. However, this approach may suffer from numerical instabilities when a large set of auxiliary basis functions (ABFs) is employed. When exx_cs_inv_thr > 0, the inversion is instead carried out via matrix diagonalization. Eigenvalues at or below exx_cs_inv_thr times the largest eigenvalue are discarded to improve numerical stability. A relatively safe and commonly recommended value is 1e-5. Force derivatives assume that modes remain on the same side of the cutoff. Eigenvalue crossings can make the truncated model nonsmooth during relaxation or molecular dynamics.

exx_v_threshold.description: See also the entry exx_pca_threshold. With the approximation , the four-center integral in Fock exchange is expressed as , where is a double-center integral. Smaller values of the V matrix can be truncated to accelerate calculation. The larger the threshold is, the faster the calculation and the lower the accuracy. A relatively safe choice of the value is 0, i.e. no truncation.

exx_dm_threshold.description: The Fock exchange can be expressed as where D is the density matrix. Smaller values of the density matrix can be truncated to accelerate calculation. The larger the threshold is, the faster the calculation and the lower the accuracy. A relatively safe choice of the value is 1e-4. LR-TDDFT exchange operators and excited-state force contractions retain all density blocks to preserve linearity; this threshold still applies to the ground-state SCF.

exx_c_grad_threshold.description: See also the entry exx_pca_threshold. is used in force. Smaller components (less than exx_c_grad_threshold) of the matrix are neglected to accelerate calculation. The larger the threshold is, the faster the calculation and the lower the accuracy. A relatively safe choice of the value is 1e-4.

exx_v_grad_threshold.description: See also the entry exx_pca_threshold. With the approximation , the four-center integral in Fock exchange is expressed as , where is a double-center integral. is used in force. Smaller values of the V matrix can be truncated to accelerate calculation. The larger the threshold is, the faster the calculation and the lower the accuracy. A relatively safe choice of the value is 0, i.e. no truncation.

exx_c_grad_r_threshold.description: See also the entry exx_pca_threshold. is used in stress. Smaller components (less than exx_c_grad_r_threshold) of the matrix are neglected to accelerate calculation. The larger the threshold is, the faster the calculation and the lower the accuracy. A relatively safe choice of the value is 1e-4.

exx_v_grad_r_threshold.description: See also the entry exx_pca_threshold. With the approximation , the four-center integral in Fock exchange is expressed as , where is a double-center integral. is used in force and stress. Smaller values of the V matrix can be truncated to accelerate calculation. The larger the threshold is, the faster the calculation and the lower the accuracy. A relatively safe choice of the value is 0, i.e. no truncation.

exx_ccp_rmesh_times.description: This parameter determines how many times larger the radial mesh required for calculating Columb potential is to that of atomic orbitals. The value should be larger than 0. Reducing this value can effectively increase the speed of self-consistent calculations using hybrid functionals.

exx_opt_orb_lmax.description: The maximum l of the spherical Bessel functions, when the radial part of opt-ABFs are generated as linear combinations of spherical Bessel functions. A reasonable choice is 2.

exx_opt_orb_ecut.description: The cut-off of plane wave expansion, when the plane wave basis is used to optimize the radial ABFs. A reasonable choice is 60.

exx_opt_orb_tolerence.description: The threshold when solving for the zeros of spherical Bessel functions. A reasonable choice is 1e-12.

exx_real_number.description:
* True: Enforce LibRI to use double data type.
* False: Enforce LibRI to use complex data type. Setting it to True can effectively improve the speed of self-consistent calculations with hybrid functionals.
* LCAO RT-TDDFT exact exchange with td_stype=2 requires exx_real_number=0 to represent the input density phase.

exx_singularity_correction.description:
Scheme for Coulomb singularity / zero-transfer treatment in exact exchange.
* limits: use the finite screened Coulomb-kernel limit, without an auxiliary correction. Default for HSE and cwp22 in both PW and LCAO. PW requires screened exchange and exx_gamma_extra=false; the latter defaults to false for this scheme.
* gygi: retain the historical PW Gygi-Baldereschi auxiliary-function correction. PW only; default for unscreened PW hybrids. For independent-k screened hybrid NSCF this can cause discontinuities at source k points.
* spencer: LCAO spherical truncation, Phys. Rev. B 77, 193110 (2008).
* revised_spencer: LCAO, Phys. Rev. Mater. 5, 013807 (2021).
* massidda / carrier: LCAO auxiliary singularity corrections.
Use the same scheme for consistent SCF and NSCF bands. A source configuration mismatch produces a warning and does not prevent reading the existing SCF files.

rpa_ccp_rmesh_times.description: How many times larger the radial mesh required is to that of atomic orbitals in the postprocess calculation of the bare Coulomb matrix for RPA, GW, etc.

rpa_cut_coulomb.description: Post-SCF cut-Coulomb kernel: hard preserves Spencer truncation; log_erfc uses erfc(log(r/Rc)/log(rpa_cut_width))/2r. Applies to Fock components in compressed and uncompressed cut exports; Erfc components retain their existing kernel. Non-default kernel/radius requests require a Fock component. Full Coulomb is unchanged. Forces and stresses for log_erfc are not validated.

rpa_cut_radius.description: legacy preserves the existing cutoff radius. inscribed uses half the shortest nonzero BvK superlattice vector, including the lattice scale in Bohr. Applies only to Fock components; inscribed is rejected if the RPA Coulomb configuration has no Fock component. Independent of rpa_cut_coulomb; intended for controlled radius-versus-smoothing comparisons.

rpa_cut_width.description: Width factor for log_erfc. Must be finite and greater than 1 and at most 1.25. The default matches the logged Si FHI-aims width; it is not a universal FHI-aims constant. The finite radial integration range must resolve the smooth tail.

exx_symmetry_realspace.description:
* False: only rotate k-space density matrix D(k) from irreducible k-points to accelerate diagonalization
* True: rotate both D(k) and Hexx(R) to accelerate both diagonalization and EXX calculation
For multi-k calculations, D(k) is averaged over the unitary little group of each irreducible k point before star expansion, for either setting.
exx_symmetry_realspace.availability: symmetry==1 and (dft_functional in [hse, hf, pbe0, scan0] or (basis_type==lcao and rpa==true))

out_ri_cv.description: Whether to output the coefficient tensor C(R) and ABFs-representation Coulomb matrix V(R) for each atom pair and cell in real space.

out_unshrinked_v.description: whether to output the large Vq matrix in unshrinked auxiliary basis

exx_coul_moment.description: whether to use moment method for Coulomb calculation

exx_rotate_abfs.description: whether to rotate auxiliary basis for Coulomb calculation

exx_multip_moments_threshold.description: threshold to screen multipole moments in Coulomb calculation

shrink_abfs_pca_thr.description: threshold to shrink auxiliary basis for GW/RPA

shrink_lu_inv_thr.description: threshold to get inverse of overlap matrix by LU decomposition in auxiliary basis representation

dft_plus_u.description:
Determines whether to calculate the plus U correction, which is especially important for correlated electrons.
* 1: Calculate plus U correction with radius-adjustable localized projections (with parameter onsite_radius).
* 2: Calculate plus U correction using first zeta of NAOs as projections (this is old method for testing).
* 0: Do not calculate plus U correction.

dft_plus_dmft.description: Whether to enable DFT+DMFT calculation. True: DFT+DMFT; False: standard DFT calculation.

orbital_corr.syntax: Vector of Integer (n values where n is the number of atomic types)
orbital_corr.description:
Specifies which orbits need plus U correction for each atom type ( for atom type 1, 2, 3, respectively).
* -1: The plus U correction will not be calculated for this atom.
* 1: For p-electron orbits, the plus U correction is needed.
* 2: For d-electron orbits, the plus U correction is needed.
* 3: For f-electron orbits, the plus U correction is needed.

hubbard_u.syntax: Vector of Real (n values where n is the number of atomic types)
hubbard_u.description:
Specifies the Hubbard Coulomb interaction parameter U (eV) in plus U correction, which should be specified for each atom unless the Yukawa potential is used.

[NOTE] Note: Since only the simplified scheme by Duradev is implemented, the 'U' here is actually U-effective, which is given by Hubbard U minus Hund J.

yukawa_potential.description:
Determines whether to use the local screen Coulomb potential method to calculate the values of U and J.
* True: hubbard_u does not need to be specified.
* False: hubbard_u does need to be specified.

yukawa_lambda.description: The screen length of Yukawa potential. If left to default, the screen length will be calculated as an average of the entire system. It's better to stick to the default setting unless there is a very good reason.

uramping.description: Once uramping > 0.15 eV. DFT+U calculations will start SCF with U = 0 eV, namely normal LDA/PBE calculations. Once SCF restarts when drho<mixing_restart, U value will increase by uramping eV. SCF will repeat above calcuations until U values reach target defined in hubbard_u. As for uramping=1.0 eV, the recommendations of mixing_restart is around 5e-4.

init_occ_mat.description:
The parameter controls how the DFT+U occupation matrix is initialized.
* 0: No occupation-matrix initialization is performed, and the onsite density matrix will be calculated from wavefunctions in each SCF step.
* 1: The first SCF step will use an initial density matrix read from a file, but for later steps, the onsite density matrix will be updated.
* 2: The same onsite density matrix read from the file will be used throughout the entire calculation.

[NOTE] The occupation-matrix file is read from the directory specified by read_file_dir. The search order is dm_onsite_ini.txt -> occ_mat.txt. Input must use the current compact format written by ABACUS; legacy Atom=/L=/spin= files such as dm_onsite.txt are not supported. The easiest way to obtain a valid file is to run a DFT+U calculation with out_occ_mat=1 (the default); the resulting occ_mat.txt in the OUT.prefix directory (which always holds the occupation matrix of the latest electronic step) can be placed in read_file_dir as-is. When out_freq_ion is positive, separate occ_matg{geom_step}.txt files are also written, one per output ionic step; they may contain several electronic-step sections separated by comment headers.

omc.description: Legacy alias for init_occ_mat with the same meaning. If both omc and init_occ_mat are present, init_occ_mat takes precedence.

onsite_radius.description:
Cutoff radius for numerical atomic orbitals used in onsite projections.
* Controls the localized projections for `dft_plus_u=1` and spin constraints (`sc_mag_switch=true`) in PW and LCAO calculations.
* Enables onsite population analysis in ordinary PW calculations when set to a positive value.
* Controls atomic magnetic moment projections for `nspin=4` PW RT-TDDFT with `td_out_mag=onsite`.

When omitted, the value is `3.0` for `dft_plus_u=1`, `sc_mag_switch=true`, or `nspin=4` PW RT-TDDFT with `td_out_mag=onsite`; otherwise it is `0.0`. Explicit values must be positive.

Provide numerical atomic orbital files through `NUMERICAL_ORBITAL` in `STRU`, with their directory specified by `orbital_dir`. Projected magnetic moments depend on the chosen orbitals and radius.
onsite_radius.default: `3.0` for `dft_plus_u=1`, `sc_mag_switch=true`, or `nspin=4` PW RT-TDDFT with `td_out_mag=onsite`; `0.0` otherwise

sc_mag_switch.description: Switch to control spin-constrained DFT calculation

decay_grad_switch.description: Switch to control gradient break condition in spin-constrained DFT

sc_thr.description: Convergence criterion of spin-constrained iteration (RMS) in uB

alpha_trial.description: Initial trial step size for lambda in eV/uB^2

sccut.description: Maximal step size for lambda in eV/uB

sc_drop_thr.description: Convergence criterion ratio of lambda iteration in Spin-constrained DFT

sc_scf_thr.description: Density error threshold for inner loop of spin-constrained SCF

sc_direction_only.description:
When true, only the direction of the magnetic moment is constrained to the target direction, while the magnitude is allowed to vary freely. This is useful for studying magnetic anisotropy or when the magnitude of the moment is determined by the electronic structure rather than an external constraint.

When false (default), both the direction and magnitude of the magnetic moment are constrained to the target values.

sc_lambda_strategy.description:
Lambda update strategy for spin-constrained DFT:
* bfgs: BFGS quasi-Newton method
* linear_response: linear response (Scheme B)
* augmented_lagrangian: augmented Lagrangian (Scheme C)
* hybrid_delayed: hybrid delayed update (Scheme D)
* linear_scan: linear sweep of lambda for testing magnetic moment response

sc_scan_lambda_start.description: Starting lambda value for linear_scan strategy. Only used when sc_lambda_strategy=linear_scan.

sc_scan_lambda_end.description: Ending lambda value for linear_scan strategy. Only used when sc_lambda_strategy=linear_scan.

sc_scan_steps.description: Number of lambda values to scan. Only used when sc_lambda_strategy=linear_scan.

qo_switch.description: Whether to let ABACUS output QO analysis required files

qo_basis.description:
Type of QO basis function:
* hydrogen: hydrogen-like basis
* pswfc: read basis from pseudopotential
* szv: single-zeta valence basis

qo_strategy.syntax: Vector of String (1 or n values where n is the number of atomic types)
qo_strategy.description: Strategy to generate radial orbitals for QO analysis. For hydrogen: energy-valence, for pswfc and szv: all
qo_strategy.default: for hydrogen: energy-valence, for pswfc and szv: all

qo_screening_coeff.syntax: Vector of Real (n values where n is the number of atomic types; 1 value allowed for qo_basis=pswfc)
qo_screening_coeff.description: The screening coefficient for each atom type to rescale the shape of radial orbitals

qo_thr.description: The convergence threshold determining the cutoff of generated orbital. Lower threshold will yield orbital with larger cutoff radius.

pexsi_npole.description: The number of poles used in the pole expansion method, should be a even number.

pexsi_inertia.description: Whether inertia counting is used at the very beginning.

pexsi_nmax.description: Maximum number of PEXSI iterations after each inertia counting procedure.

pexsi_comm.description: Whether to construct PSelInv communication pattern.

pexsi_storage.description: Whether to use symmetric storage space used by the Selected Inversion algorithm for symmetric matrices.

pexsi_ordering.description: Ordering strategy for factorization and selected inversion. 0: Parallel ordering using ParMETIS, 1: Sequential ordering using METIS, 2: Multiple minimum degree ordering

pexsi_row_ordering.description: Row permutation strategy for factorization and selected inversion, 0: No row permutation, 1: Make the diagonal entry of the matrix larger than the off-diagonal entries.

pexsi_nproc.description: Number of processors for PARMETIS. Only used if pexsi_ordering == 0.

pexsi_trans.description: Whether to factorize the transpose of the matrix.

pexsi_method.description: The pole expansion method to be used. 1 for Cauchy Contour Integral method, 2 for Moussa optimized method.

pexsi_nproc_pole.description: The point parallelizaion of PEXSI. Recommend two points parallelization.

pexsi_temp.description: Temperature in Fermi-Dirac distribution, in Ry, should have the same effect as the smearing sigma when smearing method is set to Fermi-Dirac.

pexsi_gap.description: Spectral gap, this can be set to be 0 in most cases.

pexsi_delta_e.description: Upper bound for the spectral radius of S^{-1}H.

pexsi_mu_lower.description: Initial guess of lower bound for mu.

pexsi_mu_upper.description: Initial guess of upper bound for mu.

pexsi_mu.description: Initial guess for mu (for the solver).

pexsi_mu_thr.description: Stopping criterion in terms of the chemical potential for the inertia counting procedure.

pexsi_mu_expand.description: If the chemical potential is not in the initial interval, the interval is expanded by this value.

pexsi_mu_guard.description: Safe guard criterion in terms of the chemical potential to reinvoke the inertia counting procedure.

pexsi_elec_thr.description: Stopping criterion of the PEXSI iteration in terms of the number of electrons compared to numElectronExact.

pexsi_zero_thr.description: if the absolute value of CCS matrix element is less than this value, it will be considered as zero.

out_alllog.description:
Whether to print information into individual logs from all ranks in an MPI run.
* True: Information from each rank will be written into individual files named OUT.{calculation}_{suffix}/running_${calculation}.log.

t_in_h.description:
Specify whether to include kinetic term in obtaining the Hamiltonian matrix.
* 0: No.
* 1: Yes.

vl_in_h.description:
Specify whether to include local pseudopotential term in obtaining the Hamiltonian matrix.
* 0: No.
* 1: Yes.

vnl_in_h.description:
Specify whether to include non-local pseudopotential term in obtaining the Hamiltonian matrix.
* 0: No.
* 1: Yes.

vh_in_h.description:
Specify whether to include Hartree potential term in obtaining the Hamiltonian matrix.
* 0: No.
* 1: Yes.

vion_in_h.description:
Specify whether to include local ionic potential term in obtaining the Hamiltonian matrix.
* 0: No.
* 1: Yes.

test_force.description:
Specify whether to output the detailed components in forces.
* 0: No.
* 1: Yes.

test_stress.description:
Specify whether to output the detailed components in stress.
* 0: No.
* 1: Yes.

test_skip_ewald.description:
Specify whether to skip the calculation of the ewald energy.
* 0: No.
* 1: Yes.

ri_hartree_benchmark.description: Whether to use the RI approximation for the Hartree term in LR-TDDFT for benchmark (with FHI-aims/ABACUS read-in style)

aims_nbasis.description: Atomic basis set size for each atom type (with the same order as in STRU) in FHI-aims.
aims_nbasis.default: {} (empty list, where ABACUS use its own basis set size)

rdmft.description: Whether to perform rdmft calculation (reduced density matrix funcional theory). The physical quantities that RDMFT temporarily expects to output are the kinetic energy, total energy, and 1-RDM of the system in the ground state, etc.

rdmft_power_alpha.description: The alpha parameter of power-functional(or other exx-type/hybrid functionals) which used in RDMFT, g(occ_number) = occ_number^alpha

exxace.description:
Whether to use the ACE method (https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.6b00092) to accelerate the calculation the Fock exchange matrix. Should be set to true most of the time.
* True: Use the ACE method to calculate the Fock exchange operator.
* False: Use the traditional method to calculate the Fock exchange operator.

exx_gamma_extra.description: Whether to use the gamma point extrapolation method to calculate the Fock exchange operator. See https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.79.205114 for details. Defaults to false for PW exx_singularity_correction=limits (finite screened kernel), and true otherwise. Explicit true is incompatible with the PW limits scheme.
exx_gamma_extra.default: False for PW limits; True otherwise

ecutexx.description: The energy cutoff for EXX (Fock) exchange operator in plane wave basis calculations. The pair-density G-sphere of the exchange operator, the EXX energy, and the EXX stress are all truncated at this value. If ecutexx yields a smaller FFT box and every |k+G|^2 of the wavefunctions fits inside it (i.e. ecutexx should not be smaller than ecutwfc), all EXX FFTs run on that smaller grid (QE ecutfock-style), which can significantly accelerate EXX computations. If the small grid is not usable (box not smaller, wavefunctions do not fit, or the FFT box is distributed over MPI), a warning is printed and the full grid is used. Reducing ecutexx below ecutrho reduces the numerical accuracy of the exchange contribution.

exx_batch_size.description: Number of bands processed per round of the EXX batched FFT path. 0 (the default) processes all bands in one round, which is fastest but needs nbands * nxyz work buffers; a positive value processes the bands in chunks of that width, trading some performance for a proportionally smaller memory footprint. The result is independent of the chunking.

exx_thr_type.description:
The type of threshold used to judge whether the outer loop has converged in the separate loop EXX calculation.
* energy: use the change of exact exchange energy to judge convergence.
* density: if the change of charge density difference between two successive outer loop iterations is seen as converged according to scf_thr, then the outer loop is seen as converged.

exx_ene_thr.description: The threshold for the change of exact exchange energy to judge convergence of the outer loop in the separate loop EXX calculation.
